# Riot Commander - Item Ledger

> **CITATION CAVEAT (measured 2026-07-18) - about half the commit hashes cited for
> 2026-04 through 2026-06 do NOT resolve in this repo. This is a known, bounded,
> already-self-corrected defect. Do not chase them.**
>
> Measured across `docs/history_notes.md` + `docs/LEDGER.md` + `docs/ROADMAP_HISTORY.md`:
> 387 of 1148 distinct 8-hex citations (34 percent) fail `git rev-parse --verify`.
> They are NOT scattered rot and NOT a history rewrite - a rewrite would be 100 percent
> before a cutoff and 0 percent after. The real distribution is a steady rate that
> stops dead:
>
> | month | resolvable | missing | miss rate |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 2026-04 | 1 | 3 | 75% |
> | 2026-05 | 53 | 48 | 47% |
> | 2026-06 | 452 | 457 | 50% |
> | 2026-07 | 537 | 0 | **0%** |
>
> **Cause:** the orchestrator workflow (worktree build agents, one merger) had agents
> commit inside their own worktree, and the merger cherry-picked the result. Entries
> then cited BOTH hashes - e.g. "merge `91b6b847` (slice `03927664`, worktree agent)".
> The merge hash entered `main` and resolves; the slice hash never did and never will.
> `git rev-list --all` equals `HEAD` (3645), so the slice objects are not hiding on
> another ref or in the reflog - they are gone.
>
> **The work still landed.** A dead slice hash does not mean the change is missing; it
> means that entry cited the pre-cherry-pick hash. Verify by the MERGE hash, the file,
> or the test - never by the slice hash.
>
> **Already fixed going forward:** 0 of 537 citations dated 2026-07 are unresolvable, so
> the convention corrected itself. No process change is needed.
>
> **Deliberately NOT repaired in place.** The correct hashes are unrecoverable, and
> rewriting 387 historical citations would violate the append-only rule these files run
> on. This note is additive. It exists because the defect has already cost real work:
> a 2026-07-18 audit spent a full agent trying to resolve `541cd9d3` to disambiguate a
> live-gated row, and that hash is simply gone.

1350. DONE **2026-09-06 (LANE 10 queue cycle 12 - single-row execution, inline TDD with five destructive-then-restored mutations, a read-only sibling-sweep subagent, and an independent verifier gate; Tier-1, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump, no `:8860` bounce, no Share sync, no `web/` change, no frozen file touched).** **RM-359 shipped: the rune download path is validated, and the sibling sweep found a HIGHER-severity instance in the daily-scheduled twin - refuting the filed row's own severity reducer.**

**THE DEFECT.** `lib/icons/downloader.py` carries `_safe_basename` (`:36`) with an explicit audit rationale naming a DDragon MITM. Three of its four download methods route the wire value through it - `champions()` `:122`, `spells()` `:139`, `items()` `:156`. `runes()` did not, taking `tree.get("icon")` and `rune.get("icon")` raw and building BOTH halves from them: `url = f"{DDRAGON_CDN}/img/{icon}"` and `target = out / Path(icon).name`. The classic three-of-four adoption gap, which review misses precisely because the odd one out reads naturally.

**`Path(x).name` LOOKS like sanitisation and is not - re-measured with the project interpreter rather than inherited from the row.** `Path(".").name` is `''`, so `target` becomes the `data/icons/rune` DIRECTORY itself; `Path("..").name` is `'..'`, resolving one level above it; `Path("../../etc/passwd").name` is `'passwd'`, genuinely flattened. **The row said the `.` case raises an uncaught `OSError`, and that is correct but imprecise - measured here it is `PermissionError [WinError 5]` out of `os.replace` at `lib/icons/downloader.py:33`, an `OSError` SUBCLASS whose exact type is platform-dependent** (Linux would give `IsADirectoryError`). Either way it escapes `runes()` and `download_all()`, so one poisoned entry aborts the whole icon refresh.

**THE ROW DID NOT NAME THE URL HALF, AND IT IS A SEPARATE EXPOSURE.** The three guarded siblings build their URL from the VALIDATED basename (`:127`, `:144`, `:161`); `runes()` interpolated the raw string, so a hostile `icon` escaped the `/img/` prefix of the outbound request even in the cases where the on-disk path flattened to something harmless. Both halves are now built from the validated value.

**THE FIX IS `_safe_relpath`, NOT `_safe_basename`, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW.** Real DDragon rune icons are multi-segment by design (`perk-images/Styles/Domination/Electrocute/Electrocute.png`), so applying `_safe_basename` to the whole string rejects EVERY legitimate rune and turns `runes()` into a permanent no-op - and silently, because a count of 0 reads as an empty payload. The live twin had already solved this: `tools/ddragon_mirror_refresh.py:217` `_safe_relpath` splits on `/` and requires every SEGMENT to pass `_safe_basename`. That is what was ported. `test_a_legitimate_multi_segment_rune_icon_is_still_downloaded` exists so a later "unification" pass cannot collapse the two validators; deleting the guard and deleting the feature must not look the same to the suite.

**THE ACCEPTANCE COULD NOT BE MET LITERALLY, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY SUBSTITUTED.** The row's acceptance asks for a test that `runes()` rejects an icon which "is `"."`, `".."`, **or contains a separator**". The first two are met exactly. The third CONTRADICTS the fix the row itself recommends two paragraphs earlier ("port `_safe_relpath` into `runes()`"), because `_safe_relpath` exists precisely to ACCEPT separators; implementing it literally would have shipped a function that downloads nothing. Read against its own parenthetical - "the way `champions()` already rejects `"../../x.png"`" - the intent is traversal, and `../../x.png` IS rejected. So: two clauses met literally, the third met in intent and deliberately not in letter.

**THE SIBLING SWEEP FOUND A LIVE ONE, AND IT REFUTES THE ROW'S OWN SEVERITY REDUCER #2.** The filed body states "**The live twin is CORRECT** ... So the mirror refresh that actually runs is guarded; only the unused library copy diverges." **That is now measured FALSE.** `tools/ddragon_mirror_refresh.py` guards its icons (`_safe_basename` on all eight image names in `enumerate_assets`, `_safe_relpath` on both rune paths) and its version (`validate_version`), but `champion_key` - a raw key off the downloaded `champion.json` bundle, `pull_all_champion_details:412` `list((summary or {}).get("data", {}).keys())` - reached BOTH `url = f"{DDRAGON_BASE}/cdn/{version}/data/{LOCALE}/champion/{champion_key}.json"` (`:375`) and `dest = META_DIR / version / "champion_detail" / f"{champion_key}.json"` (`:385` in the puller, `:397` in the cache-read entry point) with nothing applied. `_atomic_write_json` (`:188`) does `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` BEFORE writing, so a key of `../../../pwned` creates the escaped directory and writes into it. **Same root cause, same file family, and strictly HIGHER severity than the row that found it:** `lib/icons/downloader.py` has zero production callers, whereas this module is scheduled task `RC-DDragonMirrorRefresh`, **verified Ready on this box with `Get-ScheduledTask`** and running `--check-changed` daily at 03:30, which does NOT short-circuit `run()` (`main()` only skips for `--check-only`, `:798`; the verifier additionally confirmed `run()` calls `pull_all_champion_details` unconditionally at `:597`, so the guarded code is genuinely on the daily path). Fixed in the same commit, since section 6 step 3 makes same-root-cause siblings in scope and since leaving it would have shipped a ledger entry repeating a refuted premise.

1349. DONE **2026-09-06 (LANE 10 queue cycle 11, pushed to `main` as `77e0e290f`, fast-forward over `21acbb95c` with no force and no amend - the rebase onto `origin/main` was a NO-OP because that ref was still exactly this commit's parent, so the tree both suites ran against is byte-identical to the tree that was pushed - single-row execution, inline TDD with six destructive-then-restored mutations plus an independent adversarial verifier gate; Tier-1, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump, no `:8860` bounce, no Share mirror touched, no `web/` change, NO FROZEN FILE TOUCHED, no RC restart) - RM-358 SHIPPED-PARTIAL and RM-365 CLOSED-AS-DUPLICATE: source prose called the LCU connection pool DEFAULT-OFF for two months after it was flipped ON, and that exact comment had already mis-graded a live defect as latent.**

**THE DEFECT.** The E7 flip on 2026-06-30, validated over a live game on 2026-07-01 (LEDGER item-709), made `RC_LCU_POOL` default-ON: `core/lcu_pool.py:77` reads `os.environ.get("RC_LCU_POOL", "1")`, and `tests/test_port_cpu_footprint_rc2.py:29-33` has asserted the pool is on for an unset env ever since. A stale comment that DOWNGRADES a live defect is a process hazard, not cosmetics, which is why a Tier-0-looking row was worth a guard.

**GROUND TRUTH RE-PROBED - AND THE ROW'S CITATIONS WERE PARTLY STALE, WHICH AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS ENTRY GOT WRONG.** That draft said "all six cited `file:line` were re-opened and all six were exact". **Both halves were false and the verifier gate caught it.** The filed body (`docs/_research_refill_2026-09-05.md:548-573`) carries **8** citations, not six, and against the tree this cycle actually ran on (`21acbb95c`) **5 were exact and 3 were stale**: `core/lcu_pool.py:43` (cited for the `os.environ.get("RC_LCU_POOL", "1")` line, truly at **:77**), `core/lcu_pool.py:39-42` (truly **:73-76**) and `core/lcu_pool.py:19-20` (truly **:20-21**; `:19` is blank). **THE GUARD - `tests/test_rc_lcu_pool_default_prose_guard_rm358.py`, 11 tests, red-first.** Measured against the unfixed tree: **3 failed / 10 passed / 20 subtests**, naming both repairable sites while already recognising the frozen exemption; after the fixes, 11 passed / 22 subtests. **That red-first figure is a correction.** An earlier draft of this entry cited "3 failed / 8 passed", which was measured on a 9-test revision of the guard that was never shipped - the two `TestClaimMatcher` tests came later, after the first verifier pass. Because 3 + 8 = 11, the stale pair read exactly like a measurement of the shipped 11-test file and was undetectable without reconstructing the old revision, which is what the second gate did (`feedback_your_own_edit_staled_the_citation`: re-derive AFTER the last edit, not from memory of the first run).

It tokenizes every `.py` that mentions the flag and groups CONSECUTIVE comment lines into one prose block. **A second correction, and a more interesting one: the earlier draft claimed that grouping "is what lets it see a claim split across lines", and that a line-at-a-time scan would have missed the sentence while a whole-file scan would have false-positived on `os.environ.get("RC_LCU_POOL", ...)`. Both halves are measurably false.** All three shipped defects spell the flag name AND the claim on a SINGLE line, so a line-at-a-time scan finds the same three, and a whole-file scan finds the same three files with no false positive - `core/lcu_pool.py` carries no default-off phrase anywhere. The grouping is genuinely useful for the paraphrase where the flag ends one comment line and the claim begins the next, and the STRING-token half is load-bearing for real (`tests/test_lcu_pool.py:6` split the flag name and the claim across sentences of one docstring) - but the draft dressed a prophylactic choice up as the thing that caught the bug. That is a design rationale invented after the fact to flatter the design, and the guard's own docstring has been corrected to say so. Three design choices ARE load-bearing: (1) **the premise is DERIVED, not hardcoded** - the guard calls `pool_enabled()` with the env unset and only then demands the prose say ON, so a deliberate future flip back to OFF disarms it automatically instead of turning it into a false alarm somebody deletes; (2) **the scope is derived too** - any new module that picks up the flag is in scope the day it is written, rather than a hardcoded file list that silently stops covering the tree; (3) **the exemption registry is triple-locked** - an entry must name a file that is genuinely on the frozen list (parsed live out of `CLAUDE.md`, never copied), must still be stale, and the set is pinned, so it can be neither a silencing hatch for a fixable defect nor dead weight after the frozen half is repaired.

1348. DONE **2026-09-06 (LANE 10 queue cycle 10, pushed to `main` as `f517b2c16`, fast-forward over `6f1b268a4` with no force and no amend - the rebase onto `origin/main` was a NO-OP because that ref was still exactly this commit's parent, so the tree both suites ran against is byte-identical to the tree that was pushed - single-row execution, inline TDD with four destructive-then-restored mutations plus an independent verifier gate; Tier-1, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump, no `:8860` bounce, no Share mirror touched, no `web/` change, no frozen file touched, no RC restart) - RM-357 CLOSED: the base worker's subclass contract named a DIFFERENT CLOCK from the one its consumer differences against, so a subclass written to the documentation would have reported a dead worker as alive forever.**

**THE DEFECT.** `core/base_worker.py:34` instructed subclass authors to set `self.pulse_ts = time.time()` on each poll iteration "so HealthMonitor sees liveness". HealthMonitor does no such thing with a wall-clock stamp. `app/_health_monitor.py:55` takes `now = time.monotonic()`, `:68` computes `worker_age = (now - w_pulse) if w_pulse else 999.0`, and `:79` gates on `"game_poll_worker_alive": worker_age < 12.0`. The two clocks are different epochs: `time.monotonic()` on Windows counts from boot, `time.time()` from 1970. A subclass obeying the contract yields `worker_age` of roughly **-1.7e9**, which passes `< 12.0` unconditionally and forever. The pulse exists to detect a wedged worker; written to its own documented contract it would have reported every wedged worker as healthy - the exact inversion of the mechanism's purpose. Neither shipped subclass was affected: `core/sr_aram_worker.py:139` and `core/tft_worker.py:273` both use `time.monotonic()`, which is why nothing ever surfaced it. **This was a live trap in a class whose entire reason to exist is being subclassed**, not a typo in dead prose.

**GROUND TRUTH RE-PROBED, NOT INHERITED.** All six `file:line` citations in the filed row (`docs/_research_refill_2026-09-05.md:509-542`) were re-opened this cycle and all six were exact - `base_worker.py:34`, `sr_aram_worker.py:139`, `tft_worker.py:273`, `_health_monitor.py:55` / `:68` / `:79`. That is worth recording because it is the minority outcome for a filed row.

**THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE ONE THE ROW PROPOSED.** The row offered, as an option, "reject a non-monotonic-looking pulse in `health_pulse()`". **That guard would have shipped INERT, and measuring it is what re-aimed the fix.** `health_pulse()` has **zero PRODUCTION callers**: before this commit `grep -rn "health_pulse" --include='*.py' .` returned exactly one line in the tree, the `def` itself, and after it the only other hits are in the new test file (one of them a real call). The precise claim is zero non-test callers, and it is worded that way deliberately - an adversarial pass caught an earlier draft of this entry asserting "exactly ONE line in the entire tree", which its own commit falsified. HealthMonitor never calls it - `app/_health_monitor.py:62-63` reads `app._sr_aram_worker.pulse_ts` and `.last_success_ts` as raw attributes. A rejection placed in `health_pulse()` would have passed a test, satisfied the row's wording, and left the actual consumer reading the unguarded value (`feedback_verified_claim_vs_measured_downstream`). The guard therefore went on `pulse_ts` itself, which is the attribute the consumer genuinely reads. Two halves, both in the non-frozen `core/base_worker.py`: (1) the contract docstring now names `time.monotonic()` for `pulse_ts` AND for `last_success_ts`, and says in-line why (a wall-clock stamp makes the age negative and pins the gate open); (2) `pulse_ts` became a property whose setter routes through a new `_sanitise_pulse()`, degrading to `0.0` anything that cannot be a reading from this process's monotonic clock - non-numeric, non-finite, negative, or further in the future than `time.monotonic() + 1.0`. `0.0` is not an invented sentinel: it is the value `__init__` already used and the value `:68` already reads as "never pulsed", so a wrongly-clocked worker now reports **not alive**, which is the safe direction. The future-slack test is self-calibrating against the live clock rather than keyed to a magic epoch constant, so it does not rot.

**CONCURRENCY, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The pre-existing comment at `:49` asserted "Float writes are GIL-atomic on CPython - no lock needed", and a property turns that write into a method call. The write is still a single store to `_pulse_ts` and the read a single load, so the poll thread and the health thread cannot observe a torn value; the comment was updated to say that explicitly rather than left to imply a bare attribute.

**SIBLING SWEEP: ZERO, and the measurement is the point.** The defect class is "a contract names clock A while the consumer differences against clock B". Swept `core/ app/ dashboard/ ops/ game_reader/ coaches/ lcu/` for `time.time()` near liveness/age/pulse/stale language: 17 hits, and every one of them differences against a wall-clock source (a file `mtime`, or a `ts` written by `time.time()` in the same module), so they are internally consistent and are NOT siblings. `core/base_worker.py:34` was the only instance in the tree. Also swept every writer of `.pulse_ts`: five sites, of which two are the correct monotonic assignments and two are pass-through fields on the `WorkerResult` / `TftWorkerResult` snapshot classes. No external writer sets a wall clock. **The pre-stated prediction was 0-2 siblings and the measurement was 0** - recorded because a cycle that only finds what it went looking for is a confirmation exercise.

**BACKFILL: NOT NEEDED, and that is a measured answer rather than an omission.** This class of fix normally owes a repair of already-bad state (`CLAUDE.md` "Data Fixes"). Here there is none to repair: both shipped subclasses already pulsed monotonically, so no live worker has ever written a wall-clock `pulse_ts`, no persisted artifact carries one, and `ops/runtime/health.json` holds no pulse field. The bad state was the contract TEXT, and correcting it is the repair. The guard is prophylactic for a third subclass that does not yet exist.

**TESTS - `tests/test_base_worker_pulse_clock_rm357.py`, 18 tests, red-first.** Measured against the fully unfixed module (both production halves reverted, then restored): **14 failed / 4 passed**, including the end-to-end one; restored, 18 passed. The four that pass pre-fix are the ones that SHOULD - the good-path and never-pulsed cases, which assert the behaviour the fix must not break. An earlier draft of this entry cited "9 failed / 4 passed", which was the first red run of a 13-test revision of the file and was stale by the time the file shipped; the adversarial pass caught it and the number above was then re-measured against the final file rather than carried forward (`feedback_your_own_edit_staled_the_citation`). Supporting tests pin that a legitimate monotonic pulse still reads alive (so the guard is not over-broad), that a never-pulsed worker keeps its prior `None`/False behaviour, that both shipped subclasses still pulse on the contracted clock (a sibling guard against future drift), and that `health_pulse()` reports the guarded value.

1347. DONE **2026-09-06 (LANE 10 queue cycle 9, pushed to `main` as `42ed5ab4b`, fast-forward over `2afe2a77b` with no force and no amend - the rebase onto `origin/main` was a NO-OP because that ref was still exactly this commit's parent, so the tree both suites ran against is byte-identical to the tree that was pushed - single-row execution, inline TDD with four destructive-then-restored mutations, an independent read-only sibling sweep and an independent verifier gate; Tier-1, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump, no `:8860` bounce, no Share mirror touched, no `web/` change, no frozen file touched, no RC restart) - RM-356 CLOSED: `same_team` was unconditionally False in the non-default mode, and the flag that selects WHICH matches are returned was silently deciding what the flag MEANS.**

**THE DEFECT.** `core/pro_match_index.py` `find_pro_matches` initialized `operator_team: dict[str, int] = {}` and filled it ONLY inside `if same_team_only:`. It then read that dict unconditionally at `:122` `same_team = operator_team.get(match_id) == team_id` and emitted the result on every returned row at `:130`. Under `same_team_only=False` the dict was empty, `.get(match_id)` returned `None`, `None == team_id` is `False`, and **every** row came back `"same_team": False` - including matches where the pro genuinely shared the operator's team. The docstring at `:92-94` sold the field as meaningful in both modes. The default path was correct throughout, which is why nothing surfaced it: the filter at `:123` (`if same_team_only and not same_team: continue`) consumed the same value it had just computed correctly, so the mode that used the flag was the only mode that populated it.

**MEASURED ON THE REAL CORPUS, not asserted - this is the part worth keeping.** `data/rewind_history.db` is gitignored, so `git worktree add` never copies it (the LEDGER 989 trap); it was read read-only from the main tree's copy at `C:\Riot Commander\data\rewind_history.db` (`mode=ro` by construction - this module never writes, and nothing was written into the main tree). Over the 30-pro roster: `same_team_only=False` returns **49 matches / 62 pro-rows**. Before the fix all 62 carried `same_team: False`. After it, **29 are True and 33 are False - 29 of 62 rows, 46.8 percent, were wrong.** The 29 reconciles EXACTLY with the `same_team_only=True` mode's 29 pro-rows across 26 matches, and with the figures LEDGER 972 recorded when this module shipped ("26 matches, 29 same-team appearances, 49 matches containing any pro"). So the corrected output reproduces the historical ground truth to the row, and the two modes now agree on every match they share - the invariant the defect broke. Proving the edit happened would not have shown any of this; diffing the consumer's artifact did.

**THE FIX.** The `operator_team` query is hoisted out of the conditional and runs in both modes, with a comment recording why it must. The `same_team_only` filter at `:123` is untouched - it still selects which matches are RETURNED. The docstring gained three lines stating the separation explicitly: the flag chooses what is returned, never what `same_team` means. **The cost is one extra full table SCAN in the `False` path, NOT an indexed lookup** - this entry said "indexed" until the verifier ran `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on it and got `SCAN participants` over 30928 rows: the table is indexed on `match_id`, `champion_name` and `puuid` only, there is no index on `riot_id_game_name`, and the `lower()` wrapper would defeat a plain index even if one existed. It runs ONCE per call rather than once per pro, so it is still cheap and the fix is still right, but the correct word is scan.

**Defect.** `core/meta_crawl.py` `crawl()` carried three nested termination conditions but only two real bounds. The outer `while` (`:187` pre-fix) tests `max_players` and `max_games`, and the inner per-player `for raw_game in games:` (`:197` pre-fix) had exactly one exit, `if accumulator.total_games >= max_games: break` (`:201`). `fetcher` is typed `Callable[[str], Iterable[Any]]`, so a generator paging the service gateway is squarely in contract, and `max_players` cannot rescue the inner loop because the outer `while` is only re-tested BETWEEN players - control never returns to it.

**Root cause, stated as the class rather than the instance: a loop whose only exit is a counter that the loop body may legitimately decline to advance.** `CrawlAccumulator.record` skips `self.total_games += 1` on **five** distinct early returns (POST-fix line numbers, which is where a reader will find them today): off-family `:134`, duplicate `:138`, off-patch `:145`, malformed envelope `:123` (`_detail` returns None) and **empty-or-non-list participants `:126`**. **The filed row named two of the five. Getting from two to five took three passes, and each pass was forced by an adversarial check rather than by re-reading harder.** Reading `record` line by line found four; the verifier then asked whether `:126` was "a separate fifth shape you are still glossing", and it was - a well-formed envelope with an empty participants list is a different early return from the malformed one, and it is now tested. **The five are not uniform, and the first draft of this entry said they were.** Three (`:134`, `:138`, `:145`) `return puuids`, deliberately, since a co-player is a valid graph node either way; two (`:123`, `:126`) return `[]` - pinned independently by the pre-existing `tests/test_meta_crawl.py:120` `test_malformed_games_are_skipped_not_raised`, whose name this entry mis-cited from memory before checking. So on an unbounded stream the first three are worse than a hang - `frontier.append` (`:200` pre-fix, `:228` now) grew on every pull, making the runaway unbounded in MEMORY as well as in time - while the two malformed shapes spin without growing anything. **All five hang, which is what the bound fixes; only three leak.** The module docstring promised the opposite at `:13-14` ("repeat under explicit bounds").

**Fix.** A third bound that does not depend on anything having counted: `DEFAULT_MAX_GAMES_PER_PLAYER = 500` and a `max_games_per_player` parameter APPENDED AT THE END of `crawl()`'s signature with a default (the item-216 convention - a mid-signature insertion would break every positional call), consumed as `for examined, raw_game in enumerate(games, start=1):` plus `if examined >= max_games_per_player: break`. The default is 500 against the largest existing fixture of 60, so no ordinary crawl is truncated. Module and function docstrings now state all three bounds and say why the third is not redundant.

**A guard written in this cycle was measured INERT and DELETED rather than shipped.** The first draft clamped `per_player_cap = max(1, max_games_per_player)` so a nonsense cap could not disable the bound. Mutating the clamp away left **all 31 tests green**: the bound is tested AFTER each game is folded in and `enumerate` starts at 1, so `examined >= 0` is already true on the first pass and any cap below 1 terminates on its own. The clamp was defensive code that could never execute. It is gone, and `crawl()`'s docstring records that it was tried and refuted so the next reader does not re-add it. This is the `feedback_verified_claim_vs_measured_downstream` failure caught in the act - the line was real, committed-looking and completely without effect, and only the mutation pass distinguished it from the two guards that matter.

1345. DONE **2026-09-06 (LANE 10 queue cycle 7, pushed to `main` as `cba1d9080` - single-row execution, inline TDD with six destructive-then-restored mutations and an independent verifier gate; Tier-1, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump, no `:8860` bounce, no Share mirror touched) - RM-354 CLOSED: a bot wall is served as HTTP 200, so the scrapers' only acceptance gate passed it and it was committed over the good cached page.**

**Defect.** `lib/scrapers/_base.py` `ScraperBase.fetch` had exactly one acceptance gate, `if resp.status >= 400`. Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." interstitial, aggregator B's JS challenge and every other bot wall are served as HTTP **200**, so the interstitial cleared that gate, `_atomic_write_text` committed it over the previously good HTML, and `stamp_last_fetch(..., status="ok")` recorded success for any health probe to read. `cache_path` is only ever a WRITE target in that class - there is no read-back anywhere - so the good page was gone with no recovery path, and the two shipped targets (`aggregator D`, `aggregator B`) are exactly the kind of endpoint that serves one.

**Root cause.** Not a missing marker list: the module treated the HTTP STATUS as an acceptance test for the BODY. The fix is ordering plus a predicate - `_reject_reason(text, body)` runs BEFORE the cache write, and on rejection the cache is not touched at all, `_last_fetch.json` records the reason token, and `fetch` raises `UnacceptableBody`. That is deliberately a `RuntimeError` SUBCLASS: the sole production caller, `agents/agent2_backend/pipeline/orchestrator.py:149` and `:162`, already catches `RuntimeError` from `fetch`, so an interstitial now takes the same per-source degradation path an HTTP 500 always did, with zero caller change. Thirteen markers (`lib/scrapers/_base.py:31-45`), each a phrase specific to a challenge page rather than a bare vendor name - "cloudflare" alone would fire on any page linking a Cloudflare-hosted asset - plus a `MIN_BODY_BYTES = 512` floor for the empty and truncated 200s that carry no marker.

**Two things measured rather than assumed, both of which changed the fix.** (1) **Whole-document scanning is safe, and a head-prefix scan was the wrong instinct.** The markers were run against the six real pages cached on Legion (`data/meta_build/scraped/{aggregator D,ugg}/*.html`, 2.9M characters, 330KB-666KB each): ZERO matched, scanning each document whole. The prefix was going to exist to bound false positives on long pages; the measurement showed that risk is not real, while the hole it opens - a marker pushed past the window - is. (2) **Marker-before-floor ordering, forced by the row's own example.** The filed literal `<html><title>Just a moment...</title></html>` is **44 bytes**, under the 512-byte floor, so a floor-first order labelled the canonical bot wall `too_short_44b`. Both predicates are true of it and the token is a diagnosis a health probe reads: "bot_wall" tells an operator to back off or rotate the UA, "too_short" tells them nothing. Markers now run first.

**Mutation testing found a test that was green for the wrong reason.** Six mutations, each applied to the shipped line, run, and restored: M1 guard disabled (24 failed), M2 validate-AFTER-write - the acceptance mutation, since the raise still fires but the cache dies (20 failed), M3 case-sensitive matching (2 failed as first observed, **3 on the shipped tree** - the M3 finding below strengthened a test, so the shipped file kills that mutant harder than the run that discovered it; the verifier reproduced 3, and the number recorded here is the shipped one), M4 floor-before-markers (2 failed), M5 `MIN_BODY_BYTES = 0` (4 failed), M6 rejection stamped `"ok"` (4 failed). **M3 is the one worth recording:** `test_marker_matching_is_case_insensitive` PASSED against a case-sensitive matcher, because its 44-byte `JUST A MOMENT...` body was rejected by the length floor instead - the assertion proved nothing about casing. The body is now padded past the floor so only the marker can reject it, and the test's docstring says why. Without the mutation pass that test would have shipped as decoration.

**Sibling sweep - 2 candidates examined, 1 refuted, 1 confirmed and FILED not swept.** Swept by the root cause ("a 2xx body committed to a durable cache with no acceptance test on the body"), which meant enumerating every `get_client()` holder in the tree: `lib/ddragon/fetch.py`, `lib/icons/downloader.py`, `lib/scrapers/_base.py`. **REFUTED - `lib/ddragon/fetch.py:85-93` `_pull`** looks identical (status-only gate, then a cache write) but is NOT the same defect: `resp.json()` at `:90` parses the body BEFORE `_atomic_write_json` at `:91` and propagates `JSONDecodeError`, so an HTML bot wall, an empty body or a truncated read cannot reach that cache. **But the refutation is narrower than it first looked, and the adversarial pass is what narrowed it: the parse gates ENCODING, not SHAPE.** A 200 carrying well-formed JSON that is not the requested document - `{"error":"blocked"}` from a WAF, a bare `"maintenance"` string - parses fine and IS written over `champion.json`; `_pull` is annotated `-> dict` and validates nothing, and `_read_cached` at `:99-109` catches only `JSONDecodeError` on the file, so the poison survives every later read. Exposure is low (Riot CDN failures are HTML, which the parse does catch) but it is not zero, so calling the parse "an implicit body-acceptance gate" - the phrase this entry first carried - overstates it. The residual is folded into RM-373 as a second named site rather than given its own id. **CONFIRMED but filed as RM-373 - `lib/icons/downloader.py:82`** shares the root cause exactly, but the fix is not a mechanical extension: the payload is a binary PNG, so the predicate is magic bytes / `Content-Type`, not this HTML marker list. Exposure also differs - `:72-73` skips an existing target unless `force=True`, the host is Riot's own CDN, and `IconDownloader` has **zero production callers** (measured: the only `.py` references outside its own package are the `lib/icons/__init__.py:5` re-export, a comment at `lib/ddragon/fetch.py:66`, and one test). Filed rather than fixed per the one-row-per-cycle contract, with the differing predicate and the RM-251 collision warning written into the row. **RM-374** was also filed: the RM-354 row body carried an un-acceptanced "runner-up" (an absolute URL passed to `fetch` bypasses `base_url` while `can_fetch` still consults the ORIGINAL site's robots.txt, and `RobotFileParser.can_fetch` matches on path only) - a different root cause, deliberately not swept, and given an id so it survives its host row's closure.

**Backfill: measured, and the answer is zero bad rows - not "none needed".** Per the Data Fixes rule a hardening fix must repair the state it already allowed. All six cached pages in the main tree (`C:\Riot Commander\data\meta_build\scraped\`) were opened and run through the shipped predicate: every one is a genuine build page, 330KB-666KB, zero markers, and `_last_fetch.json` records six honest `status="ok"` stamps from 2026-04-22. Nothing to repair. Worth stating explicitly because the corpus is gitignored (`.gitignore:125`), so it is invisible to CI and a future reader cannot re-derive this from the repo.

**Tier-1 and why.** One module, local logic, no schema / engine / scorer / item-effect / `ENGINE_VERSION` surface. DS `:8860` confirmed live at `ENGINE_VERSION 1.280.0` / patch 16.15.1 before starting and was not bounced; the Share mirror is untouched. It re-derived the mutation kills itself rather than trusting the record (scratchpad-only monkeypatch scripts, zero repo writes) and reproduced all six. **The REFUTE it returned was a stale line citation in text THIS cycle authored:** the new RM-374 row cited `docs/_research_refill_2026-09-05.md:427-433` for the runner-up paragraph, but the SAME COMMIT's 6-line CLOSED banner had pushed that paragraph down to `:433-437`, so `:427` now lands mid-sentence inside RM-354's own ACCEPTANCE. **CI: `success`, read from `jobs[].steps[]` and not from the run conclusion.** `workflow_dispatch` run **34025373768**, `headSha cba1d9080c464583645cb755768ce64341e7420b` - confirmed to be this commit, not merely a descendant. The gating step `full dual suite (RM-119 - push CI now gates the whole tree)` inside the `check` job reached `completed / success`, and no step in `check` finished anything other than success or skipped. `nightly-full-suite` also passed. **Timing, since the lane's budget was re-measured twice:** `nightly-full-suite` completed at roughly 60 minutes while `check` ran on to about **86 minutes** - inside the 90-minute block, but only just, and longer than the 67 minutes RM-370 measured. Polling the RUN status alone is misleading here: the run stays `in_progress` until its slowest job ends, so the honest probe is the per-JOB status, which is what finally resolved this one.

**Suites, observed this run:** RC `tests -q -n 8` = **20783 passed, 137 skipped, 4874 subtests passed, exit 0** (236.14s); DS `agents/daemon_slayer/tests -q` = **10856 passed, 13662 subtests passed, exit 0** (118.92s). Both from the repo root, which is the pair `.github/workflows/ci.yml:504-505` runs. `ruff check .` clean; `py_compile` clean on both touched `.py` files; `tools/drift_guard.py` 0 breaches.

**A flake that looked exactly like a regression, and the experiment that got it WRONG.** The first full RC run came back `1 failed` on `tests/snapshot_panels/test_overlay_view.py::test_overlay_callouts_clamp_to_two_rows` - a file this cycle never touched. The test passed standalone, so the next step was the obvious isolation: re-run the full suite with the new test file `--ignore`d. That came back GREEN, which reads as a clean bisect - my file in, red; my file out, green - and the natural conclusion is that the new file caused it. **That conclusion would have been wrong.** Re-running the full suite on the UNCHANGED tree, with the file back in, was also green. The actual failure is `playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Page.wait_for_function: Timeout 10000ms exceeded` in a headless-Chromium overlay test - a timing failure under a loaded `-n 8` suite, the `reference_flaky_only_under_full_parallel_suite` class, and something a scrapers-module change cannot reach by any mechanism. **The lesson is about the experiment, not the flake:** on a timing-sensitive parallel suite a single-run A/B cannot separate "caused by" from "coincided with", because the control run's greenness is itself a coin flip. A deselect bisect needs repetition before it is evidence, and the cheap decisive probe - re-run the same tree unchanged - should come FIRST, since it costs one run and refutes the whole line of inquiry when it passes.

1342. DONE **2026-09-06 (LANE 10 queue cycle 4, `539b5259f` pushed to `main` - single-row execution, inline TDD with destructive-then-restored mutation testing and an independent verifier gate; Tier-1, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump, no `:8860` bounce, no Share sync, no `web/` change, no frozen file touched).** **RM-351 shipped: the shared HTTP client no longer lets a remote decide how much memory RC allocates.** **THE DEFECT.** `lib/http/client.py` read every response to EOF at two sites - the success path `body = resp.read()` and the 4xx/5xx path `body = e.read() if hasattr(e, "read") else b""` - with no `Content-Length` pre-check, no `max_bytes` parameter on `request`/`get`/`post`, and no bound anywhere in the module. **`timeout` bounds TIME, not BYTES**, which is the whole reason this survived four prior test files: a remote that keeps drip-feeding data inside the inactivity timeout never trips the timeout and streams for as long as it likes. Every DDragon bundle, every scraped page and every robots.txt lands on that line. Same amplification class lane 8 cycle 20 fixed at the `:8889` inference boundary, one layer lower and shared by every caller. **THE FIX, and the asymmetry in it is deliberate rather than an oversight.** `request` takes `max_bytes: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (16 MiB); `get`/`post` forward it for free through their existing `**kw`. A module-level `_read_bounded(reader, max_bytes)` reads in 64 KiB chunks up to `max_bytes + 1` and returns `(body, over_cap)` - the one extra byte is how an over-cap stream is DISTINGUISHED from a body that happened to end exactly at the cap, and `len(chunk)` is subtracted rather than the amount requested so a reader handing back more than it was asked for still terminates. **The 2xx path RAISES** a new `ResponseTooLarge(HttpError)`, because a truncated 200 body is a lie to the caller - `resp.json()` over half a document fails somewhere far from the real cause. **The 4xx/5xx path TRUNCATES and logs**, because that body is diagnostic only (the caller reads `resp.status`), and raising there would convert a well-formed 404 into a network-class exception AND skip the `_on_success` bookkeeping a working-but-refusing remote is owed, wrongly walking the breaker toward open. **The cap does NOT trip the breaker at all**: it is a client-side policy rejection like `Blocked`, not evidence the remote is unhealthy, and the raise lands where no handler catches it so the pre-existing `finally` releases the half-open probe slot with `settled` still False. Both of those are pinned by tests rather than left to the comment. `max_bytes=None` is an explicit opt-out; a negative cap raises `ValueError` at the call rather than silently meaning "unlimited". `ResponseTooLarge` is exported from `lib/http/__init__.py`. **16 MiB WAS SIZED AGAINST THE ACTUAL CALLERS, not picked round.** The only three consumers of `get_client()` are `lib/ddragon/fetch.py:42,72` (JSON bundles - `championFull.json` is single-digit MB), `lib/icons/downloader.py:75` (individual PNGs, KBs) and `lib/scrapers/_base.py:52,92` (robots.txt and HTML pages). The default is roughly an order of magnitude above the largest of them, so no existing caller changes behaviour, and `test_a_default_cap_constant_exists_and_is_sane` bounds it into [4 MiB, 64 MiB] so a later edit cannot quietly make it useless or absurd. **ACCEPTANCE MET LITERALLY, both clauses.** The row asked for "a test asserting `client.get(url, max_bytes=1024)` raises `HttpError` naming the cap and reads at most ~1024 bytes, given a stub opener whose `read()` yields an endless byte stream; plus a default cap so existing callers inherit it". `test_explicit_cap_raises_and_stops_reading` is exactly that, against `_EndlessResponse`, asserting the exception type, that "1024" and the url appear in the message, and that the stub served at most `1024 + READ_CHUNK_BYTES` - measured, not assumed, because the stub counts what it handed over. `test_default_cap_bounds_an_endless_stream` covers the second clause and deliberately exercises the SHIPPED default rather than a patched one, since the number that protects real callers is the one worth testing. **13 TESTS IN `tests/test_http_client_response_size_cap.py`, five of them broader than the row asked.** Beyond the two acceptance tests: `test_a_body_under_the_cap_is_returned_whole` and `test_a_body_exactly_at_the_cap_is_allowed` (the boundary is inclusive - a cap that rejected exactly-cap bodies would be an off-by-one nobody would notice), `test_max_bytes_none_disables_the_cap`, `test_a_negative_cap_is_rejected`, `test_the_cap_is_enforced_on_post_too` (the bound lives in `request`, the chokepoint - a cap written into `get` alone would leave `post` unbounded and nothing else in the tree would notice), the three `ErrorBodyCapTests` pinning the truncate-not-raise asymmetry including that a small error body is untouched, and two `CapDoesNotWedgeTheBreakerTests` proving an over-cap read leaves `failures == 0`, `opened_at is None` and `probe_in_flight` False. **`_EndlessResponse.read()` with no amount RAISES rather than hanging**, so a regression to an unbounded read fails loudly in a second instead of timing the suite out - a stub that hangs on the defect it guards is a stub that gets deleted for being flaky. **MUTATION-TESTED RED-THEN-GREEN, three mutants, each applied to the fixed file and restored through the Edit tool so every file claim stays backed by the tool record (R1).** (1) `_read_bounded` short-circuited to an unbounded `reader.read()` -> **7 of 13 red**; So FOUR of the five callers re-derived the LCU `subStyleId` themselves from the ORIGINAL name with a bare `_TREES.get(secondary, 0)`. **The verifier REFUTED an earlier wording of this entry that called all five the same mechanism, and it was right:** `coaches/rune_pages.py` computes no style id at all and contains no `_TREES` reference at HEAD - it ECHOED the requested name into the page model beside substituted perks. One root cause, two symptoms. `build_perk_ids('Conqueror', 'Precision', 'Precision')` returns `[8010, 9111, 9104, 8014, 8473, 8453, 5005, 5008, 5001]` whose slots 4-5 are Bone Plating and Revitalize - RESOLVE runes - while the caller computed subStyleId 8000, Precision. The posted page was malformed on two independent counts: subStyleId == primaryStyleId, and two foreign perks inside the named sub-tree. `_write_page` DELETES the existing RC pages BEFORE the POST, retries three times and gives up, so the operator was left with no RC rune page at all - and the only log line, `"using Resolve as secondary"`, reads as though the correction had succeeded. It had been applied to half the payload.

**FIVE call sites, one root cause.** `lcu/lcu_rune_writer._apply_runes`, `dashboard/routes_sr_draft._build_rune_cmd` (tree names arrive in a POST body), `dashboard/routes_loadout._resolve_user_build`, `coaches/loadout_resolver.resolve` and `coaches/rune_pages.resolve_page` (the name-echo site: the page displayed a tree that did not own two of its runes). Fixed root-cause-first rather than per-caller: `_substitute_colliding_secondary` is now the sole owner of the rule, `build_perk_ids` calls it so there is ONE rule rather than two copies, and the new `resolve_tree_ids` gives every site style ids that match the perks. Unknown names still resolve to 0 on that side, so each site's existing `if not sub_id` rejection is unchanged.

**REACHABILITY, stated honestly.** The two shipped recommendation files are CLEAN - measured, 164 ARAM rows and 24 SR rows, zero with primary == secondary. The reachable paths are the operator-authored ones: a POST body on the SR-draft route, and user-curated builds on the loadout routes. Dimension 4f (merely WRONG input), not 4b (abuse).

**THE MUTATION HARNESS FOUND WHAT INSPECTION DID NOT.** Reverting `dashboard/routes_loadout.py` to the pre-fix derivation left the ENTIRE suite green - nothing exercised that call site. That is `feedback_guard_on_nondefault_call_path_is_untested` exactly; two tests exist now only because the harness caught it. The one survivor, M14, was proven EQUIVALENT (an empty `RC_RUNEWRITER_POLL_SEC` reaches `float("")`, which raises into the handler that already returns the same 1.0 default) and the arm was kept because `set VAR=` is the ordinary Windows idiom for unset and should not warn.

**SECOND FIX, dimension 4d.** `POLL_INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("RC_RUNEWRITER_POLL_SEC", "1.0"))` was unvalidated in the class body. Measured both arms: `=0` yields 0.0 and `_stop_event.wait(0.0)` returns instantly (2000 waits in 0.0011s), turning the poll into an unbounded spin issuing LCU HTTP requests as fast as the client answers; a non-numeric value raises ValueError at MODULE IMPORT, which `main.py` catches as "RuneWriter init failed" (auto-apply silently off) and which also breaks the four other importers of the module. Now parsed through `_poll_interval_from_env`, which never raises, rejects nan and inf explicitly (float() accepts both, and nan fails every comparison so a naive floor check passes it through), and clamps to a 0.1s FLOOR - a floor and not a ceiling, because a deliberately slow poll is the operator's business and an unbounded spin against the game client is not.

DONE **2026-08-31 (lane 8 Headless-True-Audit cycle 38: the dashboard edge in front of the League client returned NO HTTP RESPONSE AT ALL to a one-character-wrong body, and the failure was invisible on the wire and in the log at the same time).** Tier-1: local logic in one module, no engine bump, no schema change, no Share mirror touch. Target `dashboard/routes_loadout.py` (423 -> 553 lines, NOT frozen), selected on criterion 1 (externally-reachable input: it is the LAN-reachable POST boundary that forwards operator intent into the privileged local LCU command queue). Perseus recall returned no CLOSED/REFUTED row and it has never been a lane-8 target. Filed **RM-296a-e**. **14/14 mutants killed, every restore sha256-verified.**

**THE HEADLINE, MEASURED LIVE AGAINST THE RUNNING DASHBOARD (pid 47076) BEFORE ANY EDIT.** `_serve_lcu_cmd_post` read `cmd_name = (payload.get("cmd") or "").strip()` OUTSIDE its own `try:`. `payload` is a guaranteed dict (LEDGER 1181 closed that), but its VALUES are not, and `.strip()` on a truthy non-str raises AttributeError - which nothing catches, because `_handler.py:560` calls `_dispatch.dispatch_post` in no try, `_dispatch.py` has none, and CPython's CPython `http.server` (server.py line 486) `handle_one_request` catches only `TimeoutError`. Probed on `:8888`: `{"cmd":"bogus_cmd"}` -> **HTTP 400** (correct), while `{"cmd":123}`, `{"cmd":{"a":1}}` and `{"cmd":true}` each returned **curl exit 56, http 000 - the connection closed with NO HTTP RESPONSE**. **The 400 appears in the log at `_handler.py:157`; the other three appear NOWHERE**, because the request died before the handler could log it, and the traceback goes to stderr, which under `pythonw.exe` is nowhere. Invisible on the wire and in the log simultaneously is why it survived. Fixed with a `_text()` helper that reads a string field without assuming the client sent one; the same helper closed the sibling case in `_serve_loadout_list_post` and `_serve_rune_pages_post`, which sat INSIDE their try and so turned a client type error into a 500 - a server error for a client fault, pointing the operator at logs for an RC bug that does not exist.

**FOUR MORE DEFECTS FIXED IN-SLICE.** (1) **`/api/loadout/apply` returned `{"ok": true}` when every push had failed.** `_enqueue` swallowed each exception and appended to `queued` only on success, but `ok` was hardcoded. **This is not cosmetic: `web/js/panels/item_build.js:445` ALREADY reads the field** - `if (!data || !data.ok) { _ibSetStatus("push failed", "err"); return; }` - so the operator was shown a green tick for a build that never reached the League client, and the panel's own failure branch had been dead since it was written. `ok` is now `not failed`, a `failed` list is returned alongside `queued`, and the fix ACTIVATES existing UI rather than needing any. `champ_select.js:3366` discards the body, so nothing else moves. (2) **Validate-stripped, forward-unstripped:** the allowlist checked the STRIPPED verb and then forwarded the payload untouched, so `{"cmd":" accept_ready "}` passed this edge and reached `lcu_agent.py:422`, whose `name == "accept_ready"` is False - the agent answered "unknown cmd" for a command the dashboard had already reported as accepted. (3) **Raw exception text was being painted into champ select.** `tools/lcu_agent.py:1694` fills `err` with `f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"`, `vision_server/_http.py:148` returns the record verbatim on 200, this route forwarded it, and `champ_select.js:1330-1331` renders `"X Lock failed: " + err`. A `PermissionError: [WinError 5] <path>` therefore reached the lock button - the absolute CLAUDE.md "Error Handling" rule. `_scrub_result_err` now logs the raw text and substitutes an actionable degraded line, passing `ok` and every other field through untouched, and is a transparent pass-through for any body it does not recognise. (4) **`override_summoners` admitted booleans** because `isinstance(True, int)` is True, and the two consumer paths then disagreed: the user-build path ran `int()`, the resolver path assigned the raw value. Replaced with `_coerce_override_summoners`, which rejects bools explicitly rather than coercing them - a client sending `true` for a spell id is malfunctioning, and silently reading it as spell 1 would push a wrong summoner instead of reporting.

**THE ADVERSARIAL PASS REFUTED TWO OF MY OWN FINDINGS AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE RECORDED IN THE CODE, NOT QUIETLY DROPPED.** (a) I filed the unclosed `urllib.error.HTTPError` as a socket leak on the hot polled path, reasoning by analogy from the cycle-11 `core/riot_api.py` leak (LEDGER 1277). **REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT:** CPython `urllib.request` (request.py lines 1333-1335) closes the socket immediately after `getresponse()` and an amt-less CPython `http.client` (client.py line 505) `read()` calls `_close_conn()`, so `e.fp.fp is None` by that point; 300 iterations against a local 404 server moved the process handle count by **zero**. The only residue is a `ResourceWarning` from `urllib.response.addbase`. The `e.close()` stayed, but the comment and the test docstring now both say HYGIENE, not leak, so no future reader can inflate it back into a security finding. **A defect class confirmed in one module is a hypothesis in the next, not a finding.** (b) I filed the error-path body forwarding as an Error-Handling breach. **REFUTED:** the upstream 404/500 bodies are already generic by design (`{"error":"pending"}`, `{"error":"internal error"}` - `vision_server/_http.py:146` / `:310`, closed by RM-150 / LEDGER 1177). The real breach was on the adjacent SUCCESS line, which the adversary found and I had missed - defect (3) above exists because the refutation was run. (c) It also scoped defect (4): the boolean never reaches the League client, because `lcu_agent.py:657` does `int(cmd.get("d", 0))` and both paths converge on spell id 1. So it is an inconsistent trust boundary, NOT a wrong-summoner bug in production, and the test docstring says so. (d) And it corrected my central security claim: I wrote that this edge is the **SOLE** gate, having verified the vision server does no validation whatever (`_http.py:213` -> `_relay.lcu_queue_command`, which appends the dict VERBATIM; a whole-package grep for an allowlist returns nothing). True as far as it went - but `tools/lcu_agent.py` IS a second gate (name dispatch `:422`, "unknown cmd" `:1102`, per-field coercion `:657`, per-command catch `:1693-1696`). The docstring now says the vision server is a PIPE not a gate AND names the agent as the real second gate, and a mutant that reintroduces "SOLE" is killed. **The false prose was the most durable defect here:** "the vision server also revalidates" had been telling every auditor since 2026-05-01 that this boundary was defence in depth.

**ALSO CLOSED:** the two `prefix()` routes matched any suffix - measured live, `GET /api/lcu-cmd-resultXYZ?id=1` was HANDLED and `POST /api/loadout/listEVIL` answered 400 `champion required`. Both used `prefix` only to tolerate `?id=...`, so a local `path_or_query` matcher keeps that and drops the accidental suffix match; fixed in-file rather than by changing `dashboard/_matchers.prefix`, whose other callers are outside this lane's one-file scope.

**Tests: `tests/test_routes_loadout_lane8_cycle38.py`, 52 tests, red-first - 29 RED on the first run against the unmodified module, 8 characterization green.** **MUTATION-TESTED: 14 mutations, ALL 14 KILLED**, each restore sha256-verified byte-identical, `__pycache__` purged and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` on every run so the LEDGER-1200 stale-`.pyc` trap could not manufacture a false SURVIVED. **Two process findings.** The harness reported **M8 ANCHOR MISS** rather than a pass, because rewriting the docstring had moved the line it targeted - a mutation that fails to apply looks exactly like a guard nobody needs, and the anchor assertion is the only thing standing between those two readings; re-anchored as M8a/M8b/M8c, all killed. A negative rules out without pinning down (`feedback_negative_assertion_rules_out_without_pinning_down`); replaced with positional assertions that the quote is followed by "MEASURED FALSE" plus positive pins on the facts the docstring must carry.

1303. DONE **2026-08-31 (lane 8 Headless-True-Audit cycle 37: the static seed that exists so RC survives an unreachable CN endpoint was never consulted when that endpoint answered with rows RC could not USE - so a live response of junk ids replaced a good 200-record snapshot with an EMPTY one and labelled it `source="live"`).** Tier-1: local logic in two modules, no engine bump, no schema change, no Share mirror touch. Target `core/smoothed_rates_101qq.py` (580 -> 631 lines, NOT frozen), selected on criterion 1 (it parses a payload RC does not author - the Tencent `getRankDouble` endpoint) and criterion 5 (repeat offender: this lane already fixed its lock discipline at cycle 31, LEDGER 1297, and a file fixed before is where the structural problem the first fix did not reach still lives). Perseus recall returned no CLOSED/REFUTED row. Filed **RM-295**. **5/5 mutants killed, every restore hash-verified.**

**THE HEADLINE, MEASURED AGAINST THE PRE-CHANGE MODULE BEFORE ANY EDIT.** `_build_snapshot` chose its seed with `if data: _src = "live"` where `data` was the RAW ROW LIST, then ran the indexer. But the indexer SKIPS rows whose champion ids resolve to no name (neither the 65-entry static id_map nor the DDragon fallback), so a non-empty live response can yield ZERO usable records. The fallback predicate was therefore "the live source returned no ROWS" when the only predicate that makes the fallback do its job is "the live source yielded no usable RECORDS". Probed directly: prime the cache from the static seed (`{'unique_champions': 65, 'total_records': 200}`, `source="static"`), then hand the live seam one row with ids `999999/999998` and expire the TTL - the refresh publishes `{'unique_champions': 65, 'total_records': 0}` and reports `source="live"`. **A good 200-record snapshot became 0 records, the static seed was never read, and `coverage()` reported an internally inconsistent 65 champions against 0 records** - partly-healthy-looking, which is why nothing alarmed. `/api/duo-synergy` then serves an empty panel for the full `_LIVE_TTL_S` 6-hour TTL. Fixed by splitting the shared indexer out as `_rows_to_records()` and re-basing the choice on records, not rows; the static seed is now attempted whenever live yields nothing usable.

**THE SECOND DEFECT IS THE CONTRACT INVERSION THAT LET THE FIRST ONE LAND.** `_refresh` carries the comment "a failed refresh must leave the previous snapshot in place". That guarantee held ONLY when `_build_snapshot` RAISED - and `_build_snapshot` is written never to raise: its own docstring says "Silent on missing files (yields an empty snapshot)" and it swallows `OSError` and `json.JSONDecodeError`. **So the designed failure path was precisely the one that destroyed data, and the only path that honoured the stated contract was the one the builder cannot produce.** `_publish` now drops an empty rebuild over a non-empty snapshot, logs a warning naming the record count and source it kept, and re-stamps `_LOADED_AT` so the retry lands one TTL later instead of on every single read. Reproduced end to end as a transient disk failure (live source down AND `_RECORDS_PATH` pointed at a missing file): pre-fix the primed cache went to 0 records and `pair_synergy` returned None.

**THE THIRD DEFECT WEDGED THE TEST RUN THAT FOUND IT, WHICH IS THE BEST EVIDENCE IN THIS ENTRY.** `_start_background_refresh` acquired the single-flight `_REFRESH_LOCK` and only THEN constructed and started the thread whose `finally` is the ONLY thing that releases it. A refused thread (`RuntimeError: can't start new thread`, i.e. the OS is out of them) leaked the lock permanently: every later `_start_background_refresh` returned silently on the failed non-blocking acquire, so **refresh was dead forever with no signal**, and any cold start blocked on `with _REFRESH_LOCK` **forever**. It also propagated the `RuntimeError` straight out of a public accessor into `/api/duo-synergy`. The regression test demonstrated this the hard way before the fix existed - it did not fail, it HUNG, and the pytest process had to be killed (`taskkill /F /PID 40492`, never `Stop-Process`), because the leaked lock wedged the next test's cold start. The test now force-releases the lock in cleanup so a pre-fix run fails RED rather than hanging the suite. Fixed with try/except around the construct-and-start, releasing on failure and staying fail-soft; `_REFRESH_THREAD` is assigned only for a thread that actually started.

**SIBLING SWEEP: POSITIVE, AND THE SIBLING HAD ALREADY SOLVED ONE HALF.** `core/rank_tier_bench.py:15` states in its own docstring that it "mirrors core.smoothed_rates_101qq", so it was swept rather than assumed. The result cuts both ways. It is **immune to the headline defect by construction** - it loads the static grid as the BASE and overlays live cells onto it, so an empty live result cannot erase the seed. It **already carried the exact lock-release fix** for defect three, comment and all ("Release rather than leak the lock"), which means `smoothed_rates_101qq` was the module missing a fix its own stated mirror already had - `feedback_resolver_fix_is_not_a_consumer_fix`, and the same shape cycle 33 hit when the twin module had already fixed the defect found by grep. Arriving independently at the sibling's exact idiom is the strongest available check that the fix is right. But it **does share the empty-publish wipe**: `_refresh_now` publishes `grid` unconditionally, and `_load_static_grid` is fail-soft and returns `{}` on a transient read failure, so a refresh that read nothing blanked a working grid and with it the overlay stats panel. Fixed in this slice with the same guard and pinned by `test_an_empty_rebuild_does_not_wipe_a_good_grid`. Reachable regardless of the `RC_RANK_TIER_LIVE` kill switch, which defaults OFF, because the failing read is the STATIC one.

**THE CI RED WAS THIS LANE'S OWN FLAKY TEST, AND IT WAS RACY BY CONSTRUCTION.** `tests/test_smoothed_rates_101qq_lock.py::ServeStaleWhileRefreshingTests::test_refresh_result_replaces_the_stale_snapshot` failed the nightly full suite as `AssertionError: 0.77 != 0.61`. That is the STALE assertion failing, not the fresh one: the test primed 0.61, expired the TTL, pointed the live seam at an INSTANT lambda returning 0.77, and then asserted the next read was still 0.61. Nothing stopped the background refresh from publishing first, so the assertion was a race - and it lost only under the loaded parallel CI suite, passing standalone (11 passed) and passing a local `-n 8` full run, which is exactly `reference_flaky_only_under_full_parallel_suite`. The sibling test three methods above it already had the deterministic pattern: park the fetch on an `Event` so the refresh provably CANNOT publish until the stale read is done. Applied that, plus an `entered.wait()` assertion so the test cannot pass vacuously by never starting the fetch at all. Green 5 runs in a row. The test file was last touched by this lane at cycle 31, so this red was **self-inflicted, not inherited**, and is recorded as such.

**MUTATION TESTING, 5 FOR 5, WITH THE ANCHOR AND THE RESTORE BOTH ASSERTED.** M1 revert the fallback predicate to `not records and not live_rows` -> RED. M2 disable the empty-publish guard -> RED. M3 drop the lock release from the except branch -> RED. DONE **2026-08-31 (lane 8 Headless-True-Audit cycle 33: an external-feed parser promised in three separate docstrings that it never raises, and it raised on four independent paths - while the twin module it is the stated pattern for had already fixed the fifth)** - commit `54d485c7` (+ a verifier-driven follow-up) on `lane/true-audit`, NOT merged (lane 8 ships last by design). Tier-1: local logic in one module, no engine bump, no schema change, no Share mirror touch, no restart required. Target `core/augment_external_source.py` (569 -> 675 lines, not frozen), selected on criterion 1 (it parses a payload RC does not own - Overlay App E's unauthenticated data backend, plus a CommunityDragon mirror) and criterion 4 (569 lines behind a single test file). Perseus recall returned no CLOSED/REFUTED row for it. Filed **RM-291**. New file `tests/test_augment_external_source_hardening.py`, 18 tests, **11/11 mutants killed, 0 survivors**, restore digest-verified after every mutation.

**THE CONTRACT WAS STATED THREE TIMES AND WAS FALSE FOUR WAYS.** The module docstring promises "This module never raises into its callers except via the explicit `refresh_cache` ``force`` path"; `get_priors` says "Never raises - degrades to empty on every failure"; `get_augment_meta` calls itself a "never-raises accessor". Every defect below was proven by a probe BEFORE a line was edited. **(W1)** `_normalize` coerced third-party numerics with bare `int()` / `float()`. This feed demonstrably string-encodes numbers - `augment_id` arrives as a numeric STRING, which the module's own docstring records - so a `num_games` of `"1500.0"` or a `pick_rate` of `"n/a"` raised `ValueError`, which is not `AugmentSourceError` and therefore walked straight past `refresh_cache`'s handler. **(W2)** `_table_from_meta_snapshot` rebuilt the reverse index as `{k: int(v) for ...}` over whatever the cached file held, so one junk `name_index` value raised out of the never-raises accessor. **(W3)** `_current_patch` caught `OSError` only, and `read_text` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` - a `ValueError`, NOT an `OSError` - on a non-UTF-8 file. **(W4)** A `U+2192` arrow sat in a raised error string at line 153, against the repo-wide 7-bit ASCII rule; now pinned by a source-bytes test.

**W3 IS THE FOURTH SITE OF A CLASS THIS LANE ALREADY FIXED AT ITS ROOT.** `core/polled_json.py` closed exactly this in lane 8 cycle 24, and its comment names three callers - `core/cost_tracker.py:490`, `coaches/_base_coach.py:502` and `:539` - that had widened their OWN handlers rather than fixing the root. This module was a fourth instance, and it is fixed in `_current_patch` rather than in a caller, which is what that comment exists to warn against.

**THE MOST INTERESTING DEFECT WAS FOUND BY GREPPING THE ROOT CAUSE, NOT BY READING THE FILE (W6).** `json.loads` accepts `NaN` / `Infinity` / `-Infinity` by default; `isinstance(float("nan"), float)` is True, so a non-finite survives every type check in the module; every comparison against NaN is False, so the recommender's ranking degrades **silently** rather than failing; and `json.dumps` re-emits a bare `NaN` token (`allow_nan` defaults True), which makes the written cache file invalid JSON for any strict reader. `core/synergy_external_source.py:135-147` - the twin whose own docstring cites "the augment_external_source pattern" - **already guarded exactly this**, with a comment spelling out the whole failure chain. The pattern's namesake did not. Now guarded in three places: `parse_constant` at the door, `_normalize`, and both accessors (the last matters because `read_json_dict` goes through a plain `json.loads`, which accepts those literals, so a snapshot written before this fix could still have carried one in).

**THE FIX WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED PAST ONE FIELD.** A count that will not coerce degrades to 0, but `win_rate` remains the single field whose absence DROPS the row, because a junk win rate silently becoming `0.0` would score as a 0-percent augment - strictly worse than having no external prior at all. `_finite` also rejects `bool`, which `isinstance(x, (int, float))` would have accepted, so `True` no longer reads as a 100-percent win rate. Both directions are asserted, including a negative-control test that a string `"0.52"` win rate is still dropped.

**BLAST RADIUS, TRACED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `coaches/arena_coach.py:329` absorbs a raise in a broad `except Exception  # noqa: BLE001`, so there the augment recommendation silently vanished. But `core/augment_recommender.py:303-304` calls `get_priors` / `get_augment_meta` OUTSIDE its two `except (TypeError, ValueError)` blocks - those guard only the id coercions above them - so on that path it propagated.

**BACKFILL (CLAUDE.md "Data Fixes" / section 6e): NOTHING NEEDED REPAIRING, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION.** All **18** live snapshot files under `data/daemon_slayer/` (6 patch dirs x `arena_augments` / `cherry_augments` / `mayhem_augment_stats`) were strict-parsed with `parse_constant` raising: **0** carry a non-finite literal. W6 is therefore **latent, not observed in production**, and is fixed because the upstream host is not RC's to control and the twin already treats it as live. W5 (an unbounded `r.read()` against that same third-party host, in a process that runs for days) is capped at 32 MB; both real payloads are under 2 MB.

**SEVEN-DIMENSION VERDICTS.** *Correctness* HARDENED (W1-W3, the docstring contract falsified by probe before any edit). *Security* HARDENED - shape assertion at the trust boundary (W1/W2/W6); no path-traversal surface, since the only request-shaped input is the mode enum, checked against `_ENDPOINTS`, and the `patch` segment of every cache path comes from RC's own `current.txt`, not from a payload; **no secret surface at all** - this module reads no API key (0 matches for the key path), which is why its error strings can safely carry the URL. *Error handling* HARDENED - both degrade paths verified live, and nothing here renders to a user-facing panel, it logs at WARNING. *Resource lifetime* HARDENED - W5 caps the body; `urlopen` was already inside a `with` and already carried a 15 s timeout. *Input validation* HARDENED (W1/W2/W6). *Machine environment* N/A - no `RC-*` scheduled task, `.ps1` or `.bat` references this module; it is imported in-process by `coaches/arena_coach.py` and `core/augment_recommender.py` only. *Concurrency* **CLEAN, AND DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE - the obvious "fix" is the bug this lane shipped two cycles ago.** `get_priors` releases `_lock` before calling `refresh_cache`, so two threads can miss the cache and both fetch. That is benign: the fetch is idempotent and the write goes through `atomic_write_json`, so the cost is one redundant request. Closing the window would mean holding `_lock` across a 15-second network call - which is precisely the defect of LEDGER 1297 (cycle 31), where a fallback existing for an unreachable endpoint sat behind that endpoint's full timeout under a lock every reader takes. The duplicate fetch is the correct trade and is recorded so the next audit does not "fix" it.

**THE VERIFIER REFUTED A NUMBER AND TWO TESTS, AND ALL THREE WERE REAL.** (a) The backfill count was first written as **24** and is **18**: the measuring glob unioned `*augment*.json` with `cherry_augments.json`, and the second pattern is a SUBSET of the first, so every cherry file was counted twice. It had already been committed into the test docstring, so it was a durable false statement, not a chat slip - `feedback_filed_counts_are_hypotheses` landing on this lane's own artifact. It is corrected in place AND the correction is recorded there, rather than quietly swapped. (b) The body-cap test was **partially vacuous**: its stub's `read(self, n=-1)` ignored `n`, so a mutant that kept `if len(body) > cap` but reverted to an unbounded `r.read()` would still have passed - it pinned the raise and not the memory bound, which is the entire stated rationale for the cap. The stub now honours `n` and asserts `read` was called with `cap + 1`; that exact mutant is now killed. (c) The production comment claimed `_finite` rejects `bool` and no test asserted it; one does now. An earlier grep for already-poisoned rows also "found" 12 files and was wrong - it was matching `Infinity` inside augment NAMES, and the strict parse is what is reported.

**THE COLUMN THE FOLD DEPENDED ON IS NULL FOR EVERY ROW IT MATTERED FOR, AND THAT WAS MEASURED, NOT READ.** Riot does not send `itemId` on an ITEM_UNDO timeline event - it sends `beforeId` (the item held before the undo) and `afterId` (the item held after it). `scripts/rewind_scraper.py:567` maps only `ev.get("itemId")`, so `timeline_events.item_id` is NULL for **28405 of 28405** ITEM_UNDO rows in the live 1.87 GB `data/rewind_history.db`. `_build_inventory_at` guarded its undo branch on `and item`, so the branch was **structurally dead**: it could not fire, had never fired, and the module docstring nonetheless claimed "UNDO reverses the most-recent matching purchase". This is the `feedback_rendered_field_is_not_evidence_of_a_producer` shape one layer down - the consumer, the column and the schema comment all named ITEM_UNDO, and none of them carried the value.

**BOTH DIRECTIONS WERE WRONG, NOT ONE.** Classifying all 28405 rows by `raw_json`: **25917 carry `beforeId`** (an undone PURCHASE - the item was wrongly LEFT IN the inventory) and **2488 carry `afterId`** (an undone SALE - the item was wrongly LEFT OUT). A fix that only removed `beforeId` would have closed 91 percent of the defect and silently kept the rest.

**MEASURED DOWNSTREAM, NOT JUST "MY CHANGE HAPPENED"** (`feedback_verified_claim_vs_measured_downstream`). `participants.item0..item6` is ground truth for the end-of-game inventory, which makes the fold falsifiable. Over the 40 most undo-heavy matches / 400 participant-inventories, EXACT inventory reconstruction went **12 -> 37 (3.1x)** and slot-level matches 2234 -> 2261. The same figures were then re-measured against the SHIPPED module rather than the scratch prototype. **Stated honestly: 37 of 400 is still not "correct".** The residual is the component-consumption and trinket modelling that `core/replay_seek.py:29-34` already warned makes event-replay inventory error-prone; only the undo axis was in scope. **Tie-break caveat, from the verifier and recorded rather than left in chat:** matches ranked 39-41 all sit at 25 undo events, so "the 40 most undo-heavy" is ambiguous at the boundary - under the reverse tie-break the pair is **12 -> 35**. The direction and the ~3x magnitude are robust either way; the headline figure is the natural tie-break.

**THE BACKFILL WAS FREE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF READING `raw_json`** (CLAUDE.md "Data Fixes" / section 6e). The scraper stores the verbatim Riot event in `raw_json` and that column is NULL for **0 of the 28405** undo rows, so every historical row is repaired the moment the fix ships - no migration of a 1.87 GB WAL database, whose `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars make a copy-and-replace its own hazard. Verified live rather than asserted: the 12 -> 37 measurement above IS the historical repair.

**FOUR MORE DEFECTS IN THE SAME FILE, ALL LATENT AGAINST TODAY'S DATA AND ALL SAID SO.** (a) `if queue_filter:` treated queue_id **0** - a real queue, custom games - as "no filter" and silently returned every match; the corpus happens to hold no queue-0 rows today. (b) `LIMIT -1` is UNLIMITED in SQLite (measured), and `list_matches` runs one extra join PER ROW, so a negative limit was a full-table read amplified into an N+1; `dashboard/routes_coach.py:24` clamps to 1..200, so the route was safe and the function that owns the query was not. (c) The frame sampler `timestamps[int(i * len/max)]` can never reach the final index - at 90 frames capped to 60 it kept index 88 and dropped 89, losing the END of the game; the live corpus maxes at **53** frames so the cap never triggers. (d) `max_frames=0` was a ZeroDivisionError on a public signature. Each has a test; none is claimed as an active outage.

**TWO MUTATION SURVIVORS, BOTH CONVERTED TO KILLS BY STRENGTHENING, NOT EXCUSING** (`reference_mutation_survivor_may_be_equivalent`). The important one: dropping `raw_json` from the production SELECT **survived the entire suite**, because every undo test called `_build_inventory_at` with rows the test itself selected - the real `match_detail` query was never exercised, the textbook `feedback_guard_on_nondefault_call_path_is_untested`. Worse, my own defensive `except (IndexError, KeyError): return 0, 0` was MASKING it: a broken SELECT degraded silently back to the exact dead-branch bug being fixed. Fixed on both sides - a missing COLUMN now raises (a caller contract violation, not bad data) while empty or malformed `raw_json` still degrades quietly, and two end-to-end tests through `match_detail` close the path. The second survivor coerced a NULL participant id to 0, inventing a phantom participant; the test asserted `None not in inv` and passed, so it was strengthened to reject any falsy participant key.

**DIMENSIONS.** CORRECTNESS HARDENED (5 defects). INPUT VALIDATION HARDENED (limit, max_frames, queue_filter). RESOURCE LIFETIME HARDENED - both public functions already closed in a `finally`, but nothing PROVED it, so four tests inject a mid-query `sqlite3.OperationalError` and assert the handle closed on the raising, not-found and happy paths; two leak mutants kill them. SECURITY CLEAN and measured, not read: every query is parameterized (pinned by a hostile-match_id test that asserts the `matches` table survives), no request-derived paths, no secret on any path, and **zero `except Exception` in the file** - all ten handlers are narrow. ERROR HANDLING CLEAN - `dashboard/_errors.send_error` (RM-134) already scrubs, and `_limit_param` already degrades a malformed `?limit=` to the default. CONCURRENCY N/A for atomic writes (read-only module); the `match_detail` LRU is lock-guarded and `_load_champ_index` publishes its index complete, a 2026-06-11 fix that still holds. MACHINE ENVIRONMENT N/A - no scheduled task, no listener, no process of its own.
