**THE HEADLINE, and the reason it matters more than the individual defects.** `core/vision_token.py` says in its own docstring that there is "NO hardcoded fallback (the legacy default was retired by the 2026-04-28 audit, proposal 1.7): a missing token raises RuntimeError at import time so a misconfigured deploy fails loud instead of silently authenticating every request with a known constant". The resolver was hardened; **five consumers kept a private copy of the retired constant anyway** - `game_reader/poller.py:41`, `web_dashboard.py:44`, `tools/calibrate_vision.py:25`, `tools/match_monitor.py:21` and `tools/ds_matchdb_mcp_server.py:204`. That is `feedback_resolver_fix_is_not_a_consumer_fix` verbatim, and memory `reference_vision_token_canonical` already records this exact literal causing two silent-401 outages (items 242 and 243) whose only symptom under `pythonw` was a feature quietly not working. **Measured live, not inferred:** `GET :8889/latest-frame` with the retired constant returns **401**; with the canonical resolver, **200** and a 224667-byte frame.

**SEVERITY IS GRADED, AND AN ADVERSARIAL PASS CUT IT TWICE - both cuts are kept here so nobody re-inflates them.** (1) `tools/calibrate_vision.py` and `tools/match_monitor.py` held the literal UNCONDITIONALLY, with no env override and no other token path, and both genuinely call the relay from `__main__` - so both were 401ing on every request and were broken outright. But neither is imported by any module or bound to any scheduled task, so the blast radius is "an operator-run dev tool errors", NOT a runtime outage - and `calibrate_vision.py` is the tool CLAUDE.md names for expanding OCR coverage, which is the real cost. (2) The `poller.py` and `web_dashboard.py` sites are **hygiene, not live defects**: `get_vision_token()` raises RuntimeError, not ImportError, so only a physically absent module could take that branch, and a bad `RELAY_TOKEN` merely makes `_try_relay` return None, after which `read_game` falls through to the direct `:2999` path. The word "landmine" was in the first draft of the code comment and was removed after the refutation.

**THIS CLOSES A FILED DEFER, IT IS NOT A DISCOVERY.** `ops/audit/P2_FINDINGS.md:498` (item 409, 2026-06-13, MED) already named `tools/calibrate_vision.py:25` and noted the literal was "pervasive across ~12-18 files". Its sibling `tools/rc_facts.py:40` was fixed at some point without the row being updated, so that line is now half-stale. What cycle 14 adds over the 2026-06-13 filing is the part that stops recurrence: a repo-wide guard.

**THE SECOND DEFECT FAMILY IS ON A DORMANT PATH, AND SAYING SO IS THE FINDING.** `_process_champ_select` had no type guards at all - `session.get("bans", {})` returns `None` rather than the `{}` default when the key is PRESENT and null, and `read_champ_select` swallowed the resulting AttributeError. **But `read_champ_select` has ZERO production callers**, and it is the sole caller of `_ensure_lcu`, `_lcu_get` and `_process_champ_select`, so the entire LCU branch of this module is currently dead. The `_lcu_get` hits in `lcu/lcu_postgame_collector.py` are that class's OWN same-named method - `feedback_symbol_name_collision_masks_dead_code`, caught by the refutation pass and independently re-verified before it was written down. The guards shipped anyway (the path is wired to be revived and the code now matches its own docstring), but they are recorded as dormant-path hardening, not as the repair of an observed champ-select outage.

**Fixed in-slice:** the five token sites; `_process_champ_select` shape guards (null session, present-but-null `bans`, non-list team, non-dict pick entry, null ban list) via a new `_picks` helper; LCU lockfile port validation (`isdigit` plus `0 < port <= 65535`) and a non-empty auth-field check, both of which now `continue` to the next candidate lockfile instead of caching garbage for the process lifetime; and `_read_game_fallback`'s event normalisation, which was `list(ev.values())[0]` - trusting the KEY ORDER of a foreign payload, so a dict whose first value was a version string handed that string downstream as the event list. Now `_normalise_events` selects the first list-valued entry by SHAPE and returns an empty list when there is none.

**Tests: `tests/test_poller_lane8_cycle14.py`, 19 tests, the module's first dedicated coverage. ALL 11 regression guards mutation-tested red-then-green, and the mutation run earned its keep twice.** First, it caught the root-cause token guard being defeatable by the most obvious workaround: written as a contiguous-substring check, it passed against a split literal. The fix was to strengthen the GUARD (a `_despliced` pass that collapses adjacent quoted fragments), not to weaken the test - `feedback_mutation_probe_vs_naive_alternative`. Second, the harness itself produced a FALSE "SURVIVED" on the team-list guard, which manual re-application refuted; the cause was stale `__pycache__` between iterations, and purging `.pyc` files before each run made the result reproducible at 11/11. **A mutation harness that does not invalidate bytecode reports survivors that are not survivors** - the same shape as `feedback_mutation_that_fails_to_apply_looks_green`, one layer down.

**FOUR SUITE FAILURES WERE OBSERVED AND TWO WERE ARTEFACTS - the distinction was measured, not assumed.** The inherited baseline taken BEFORE any edit was 2 failed / 19191 passed (`tests/phase8_smoke/test_sr_draft_profile_engine.py::TestLiveEngineIntegration::test_live_three_profiles` and `tests/test_subagent_prompt_flag.py::test_cli_version_still_matches_the_pin`), so those two are not this cycle's. A later full run showed 4 failed, the two extras being `test_ds_share_host_dependent_tests_excluded.py::test_shipped_mirror_collects_without_error` and `snapshot_panels/test_champ_select_view.py::test_picks_target_mode_gated[sr-True]` - the second of which reads exactly like a regression from the champ-select edit. Re-run in isolation, both passed: they were collisions from three concurrent pytest processes against one worktree (a full RC run, a full DS run, and the verifier's own run). **Recorded because the alarming-looking one was in the file family just edited, which is precisely when a contended result is most likely to be believed.**

**Filed, not fixed:** RM-229 (four unbounded `json.loads(r.read())` paths in this module; graded LOW on purpose - all four peers are loopback, so it is defence in depth, and a cap is a policy choice wanting one consistent decision) and RM-230 (two residual lockfile checks in the FROZEN `lcu/lcu_client.py` - it already fails safe via `int()` inside a `ValueError` catch, so the row leads with that and must not be read as the frozen file being unguarded). A lane-7 handoff row covers `ops/tls/_bridge_msg.txt`, the last file carrying the retired literal, which lane 8 deliberately did not delete because removing tracked scratch is tree-shaped work.

**Backfill (charter 6e):** the already-bad state was two operator tools that could not authenticate. Repair verified LIVE by probing `:8889` with both tokens and comparing status codes, not by re-reading the source. **No RC restart was performed and none was applicable:** the running RC (pid 7788) executes MAIN-tree code, this branch is unmerged, and section 7 forbids writing into the main tree - so a restart would have proved nothing about this code. Runtime verification belongs to the merge. Frozen-file edits: none.

Now filtered to dicts with a string `id`, which repairs the bad state on the next reconcile. **Justification narrowed after review: `_write_pending` is the SOLE writer in the tree**, so a bad shape can only arrive externally (hand edit, truncated write, restored directory) - rare, but permanent and silent, which is what earns the filter. **W5** `_enemy_has_smite` cited a raw name the code never read (`rawDisplayName`); So the age pass had nothing to reclaim and the very next sweep to cross the cap would run the size pass over live files. **SIX WEAKNESSES, ALL CLOSED IN-SLICE.** (1) **THE HEADLINE: no file was ever exempt from deletion, including the one a live logging handler holds open.** The size pass sorted oldest-first and deleted until under cap with no exclusion of any kind. Windows refuses to unlink a file an open handle holds, which is the only reason this had not already destroyed an active log - and that accident is precisely what hid it, because the failure was swallowed at DEBUG and the sweep returned normally. `_protected_paths()` now reads `baseFilename` off every live handler (read off the handler OBJECT, never guessed from the date, because log_setup's `DailyRotatingFileHandler` rewrites `baseFilename` in place at the day roll) and pins those paths in BOTH passes; a pinned file still counts toward the cap total, it is only never a candidate. (2) Every per-file failure was logged at DEBUG and the sweep returned normally, so a retention loop that had not reclaimed a byte in weeks - the permission-denied case, i.e. the whole dir held open - was indistinguishable at INFO from a healthy one; a dir left over cap now logs a WARNING naming how much is pinned. (4) `stop()` joined with a timeout and then dropped the thread reference **unconditionally** - a sweep still walking a large dir outlived its join, the reference was lost, and the next `start()` both passed the idempotence check AND called `_stop.clear()`, resurrecting the abandoned loop; two delete loops then ran with only the newest tracked. A worker that outlives its join is now KEPT and reported, and `start()` refuses to spawn alongside it. (5) The idempotence check read `_task is not None`, so once the AppLoop task ended - cancelled, or dead on an unexpected error - the flag latched and `start()` returned early for the rest of the process lifetime, leaving retention silently off until RC restarted; it now asks the task whether it is done, and an unrecognised handle counts as RUNNING so an unknown scheduler can never cause a double spawn. (6) The success line read `(age>14d or total>100MB)`, so a live log could not say WHICH policy deleted a file - **that is not a cosmetic point: it is the exact question this audit needed to answer about 13 historical sweeps on Legion and could not.** The two passes have very different blast radii and one of them reaches inside the age window; they are now counted and reported separately. **The docstring was also wrong and the CODE was right:** the header claimed the cap deletes "past 14 days only", which would make the cap unenforceable, since the age pass has already deleted everything past 14 days. The hard-cap behaviour is authoritative and is now pinned by `test_size_pass_deletes_oldest_first_and_stops_under_cap`. **Also narrowed:** every per-file `except Exception` -> `except OSError` (`stat`/`unlink`/`glob` raise nothing else), removing four inline `noqa: BLE001` markers; the two daemon-loop catches are deliberately kept broad, because a sweep thread that dies silently is the worse failure. The file also had no `# arch:` header, so it was **absent from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` entirely** - added, which is what the pre-commit archmap hook caught. **Tests: `tests/test_log_retention.py`, 18 new, 0 skipped, red-first** - 12 red on the first run and 5 characterization green. **MUTATION-TESTED: 12 mutations, one per guarded production line, ALL 12 KILLED.** **THREE PROCESS FINDINGS, each of which produced a WRONG answer before it was caught, and together worth more than the fix.** (a) The two live-handler tests **passed VACUOUSLY on the first RED run**: Windows refuses to unlink an open file, so asserting `active.exists()` passes whether or not the module protects anything. They were rewritten to install a RECORDING spy that delegates to the real `unlink` and to assert the active path is never AMONG THE ATTEMPTED TARGETS - a raising spy would have been equally vacuous against fail-soft code (`reference_raise_based_spy_is_vacuous_under_fail_soft`). Only then did they go honestly red. The verifier independently confirmed the assertion that actually reddens under the protection mutant is `assert active not in attempted`, and that both `exists()` assertions stay true under it. (b) The mutation harness reported a **false SURVIVED for M5**, and the cause is durable: `max_age_days` and `max_total_mb` are the **same character length**, so the M4 and M5 mutants produce byte-identical FILE SIZES, and Python validates a cached `.pyc` by source mtime-in-whole-seconds plus size - written inside the same second, M5 silently loaded M4's stale bytecode, in which the `max_total_mb` guard was still intact. (c) Recovering from that investigation, `git checkout -- core/log_retention.py` was run to undo a probe and **destroyed the entire unstaged rewrite** - restored byte-exact from the harness's own copy-aside backup, which is why the harness keeps one (`reference_git_checkout_destroys_unstaged_mutation_probe`, hit live). **BACKFILL (6e) PROBED ON THE LIVE TREE, NOT ASSUMED.** The loop has fired for real: **13 `log retention: deleted` lines** across the retained logs. 1194. DONE **2026-08-04 (RM-42 follow-on: the extra shot's ON-HIT APPLICATION + its own CRIT; ENGINE 1.273.0 -> 1.274.0, Tier-2). THE ROW'S ORDERING CLAIM IS NOW REFUTED, NOT OPEN - the completed model contradicts the prediction it was built to test.** LEDGER 1193 shipped the shot's DAMAGE and recorded why the ordering did not move; this ships the two halves a damage registry cannot express, which is exactly what the row asked for. **NEW `agents/daemon_slayer/_extra_shot_overrides.py`**, one entry - Akshan Dirty Fighting, `on_hit_applications=1.0`, `can_crit=True` - authored off DDragon 16.15.1: "The additional shot applies on-hit effects, triggers on-attack effects, and can critically strike". DEFAULT-OFF `apply_extra_shot_procs`, reachable from `compute_dps`, `rank.rank_items`, `POST /dps`, `POST /rank` and BOTH client functions. **PLACEMENT IS THE CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT, not a detail.** The on-hit half scales the attack count bound INSIDE the `every_n_attacks` branch of `_periodic_proc_dps`, so a time-driven proc provably cannot be accelerated by it - pinned by a difference test on a Sunfire-only build, which is the test that would have caught the naive "multiply the whole proc sum" version. It does NOT touch `base_dps`: the extra shot's own damage belongs to `_passive_damage_overrides`, and folding it in here too would double-count one hit. The crit half multiplies the REGISTERED passive magnitude by the same `(1 + crit * crit_bonus)` the base auto uses, guarded on the entry so an every-AA passive that is not a second attack (Warwick Eternal Hunger is on-hit magic) is never scaled. **NO BESPOKE CRIT MULTIPLIER WAS AUTHORED, and that is a refusal rather than an omission:** the crit clause ships TWO bracketed variants in one string - "(22.5% + 12%) bonus damage" and "100% base damage + 30% bonus critical damage" - which are alternate tooltip renderings, not a quotable number, so the shot gets the engine's own standard crit expectation (the least-invention reading of "can critically strike"). A wiki-verified value would be a NEW FIELD, never a tuned fudge on the damage magnitude. **SCOPE IS ENFORCED, NOT DOCUMENTED:** `on_hit_applications` is a steady-state multiplier on the attack count, so a periodic shot would be over-credited; a test asserts every entry in this registry is ALSO on `_AA_ROUTED_ON_HIT_KEYS`, the same every-AA bar, so Caitlyn Headshot (every Nth) cannot be added here without failing loudly. **THE MEASURED ANSWER, AND IT REFUTES THE ROW.** Both flags armed, L16 vs the sweep-standard tanky target at depth (Kraken + Hexoptics C44 + Berserker's): weighted DPS **142.06 -> 257.05, +80.9 pct**. ON-HIT ITEMS RISE AND CRIT ITEMS DO NOT - Guinsoo's #7 -> #6, Terminus #7 -> #5, Yun Tal DOWN #6 -> #7, Hexoptics C44 #19 -> #17, Runaan's / BotRK keep #1 / #2. RM-42 predicted the opposite (on-hit drops out of the lead, Hexoptics rises to his top-4). **That prediction was an artifact of the filing's "200% crit double-shot" mis-read: the shipped text says the shot APPLIES ON-HIT, so a faithful model MUST raise on-hit value, and the more completely it is modelled the more on-hit wins.** So the row is closed as REFUTED-ON-ORDERING with the damage half shipped, not left open pending a better model. **THE NON-CLOSURE MARKER WAS WRONG AND IS REWRITTEN, NOT DELETED.** LEDGER 1193 authored `test_rm42_ordering_claim_is_NOT_closed_by_this_slice` expecting it to GO RED when this follow-on shipped. It did not go red - on-hit still leads - so the test now pins the REFUTATION under a corrected name and docstring. A marker that predicts its own death and then survives is evidence about the claim, not a stale test to quietly drop. **A GUARD EARNED ITS KEEP MID-SLICE:** `test_route_seams_reach_the_client_per_route` caught `/dps` parsing the seam while `dps_for` could not express it, and its failure message says to fix the client rather than widen the exclusion list - which is what was done. **Suites fresh from the REPO ROOT at final state:** DS **10413 passed / 6520 subtests** (`-n 8`, 38s); RC `tests/` **18225 passed / 108 skipped / 0 failed** (the single `phase8_smoke` live-integration failure is the standard pre-restart artifact and passes 18/18 after the bounce). 1190. DONE **2026-08-04 (RM-150 CLOSED: `:8889` narrowed to loopback and its 5xx bodies redacted - and the narrowing turned out to be a CLIENT sweep, not a one-line bind change; Tier-1, `vision_server` + 3 agents).** Both halves LEDGER 1177 filed rather than fixed on the way past. **HALF A - the bind.** `ThreadingHTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", PORT))` was legacy from the pre-ADR-011 2-PC era when the frame and LCU agents lived on a second machine; it now only bought LAN and tailnet reachability for a route family gated by one `X-RC-Token` header, which is the amplifier 1177 named on the `/sync/get/` traversal. Replaced by `vision_server._bind_host()` - `RC_VISION_BIND`, defaulting to `127.0.0.1`, with a **blank value treated as unset** so a scheduled task exporting an empty variable cannot silently re-open the wildcard. `tests/test_vision_server_threading_s7.py` pinned the literal by regex exactly as the row warned, so the S7 guard moved in the same commit - and it moved to pinning the CLASS (`ThreadingHTTPServer((host, PORT), Handler)`), which is what S7 was ever about, with the address pinned separately in the new file. **THE ROW'S OWN LIVE-GATE TRAP FIRED, AND THE ANSWER WAS NO.** The filing said "if any ONLOGON agent is pinned to the LAN IP the row is live-gated". Three were - `tools/lcu_agent.py:62`, `tools/screen_agent.py:59`, `tools/phase_watcher.py:47`, all `http://192.168.8.230:8889` - but that makes it a code sweep, not a game: only `lcu_agent` is scheduled (`RC-LCUAgent`), the other two are served-and-installable, and all three were repointed to loopback with an env override on the in-tree `tools/liveclient_relay._upload_url` precedent (LEDGER 1183), which had already made this exact move for the fourth agent and recorded the reasoning - same machine, so the token crossed the LAN interface in cleartext for nothing, and a DHCP change would have killed the agent silently under `pythonw`. **The durable generalization: a wildcard bind HIDES its clients, so narrowing one is a client sweep first.** Guarded by an allowlist-driven test that reads `_AGENT_ALLOWED` off `dashboard/routes_static.py` and refuses the LAN literal in every served `tools/*.py` - the same allowlist-driven shape that found the fourth token file in `test_agent_relay_audit.py`, chosen because a hand-listed sweep would not have caught `phase_watcher` and did not, the first time. A stale endpoint list in `lcu_agent`'s own module docstring was caught by that sweep, not by reading. **HALF B - the 5xx bodies.** Four `self._j(500, {"error": str(e)})` sites plus a `/monitor` 404 that returned its whole candidate list including `Path.home()`. 1177 classed this as hardening, not an Error-Handling breach (`:8889` is a machine-local JSON API, not a coach UI), and that classification is kept - it is closed because it is a free disclosure of install layout and exception internals, not because the CLAUDE.md rule binds it. One `_err500(where, exc)` helper logs `type(exc).__name__` plus the message and answers `{"error": "internal error"}`; **redaction is not suppression and the test enforces that** - it asserts all four call sites AND that the helper still logs. Authoritative, but source rather than docs, and it can move without a docs diff. **NOT IN THE FILING AND ARGUABLY WORSE: `nightly-full-suite` had LESS headroom than the job that actually failed.** Its successful wall clock measured **24m13s .. 28m08s against a 30-minute ceiling** - under two minutes - so fixing only the job that happened to blow up first would have left the identical defect one job up in the same file. I had read maxima off an aggregate instead of off the step rows. Functionally harmless - the 40m floor and 45m ceiling still clear it - but the test docstring's stated safety argument ("well above the 25m29s worst COMPLETE observation") overstated the margin by 2m11s, so it was corrected in both places rather than left as a number someone would later cite. (b) The docs claim above: I had asserted the step->failure behaviour as though documented. (c) **The verifier also found a residual I did not ask about, and it was the skip-is-green class this repo keeps getting bitten by.** `pyyaml` is test-only and absent from `requirements.txt`; `check` installs it and `nightly-full-suite` did not - so **every assertion in the new module, AND in `tests/test_ci_docs_guard_coverage.py`, silently skipped in the nightly job** while reporting a green tick. But `dashboard/routes_static.py:144-169` `_serve_agent_file` goes from allowlist check straight to `open()` with **no auth of any kind**, and `dashboard/server.py:35` binds `HOST = "::"` - so `GET /agent/liveclient_relay.py` returns 5033 bytes containing the literal, and the verifier confirmed it is reachable on **tailnet `100.70.22.55` and LAN `192.168.8.230`**, not merely loopback. Today that publishes a dead string; the day someone "fixes" the fallback by pasting the live value, it publishes the live one. **THE SIBLING SWEEP WAS DONE BY THE TEST, NOT BY ME, AND THAT IS THE REUSABLE LESSON.** My hand grep found the literal in three files. The test - which reads `_AGENT_ALLOWED` off disk via `ast` and parametrizes over it - found **four**, catching `tools/phase_watcher.py` that I had missed because I only checked the names I had happened to eyeball. All four now return `""`. **FINDING 3 - the upload target was a hardcoded LAN IP.** `http://192.168.8.230:8889` still resolves on this box, so it worked, but post-ADR-011 both ends are the SAME machine: the `X-RC-Token` was crossing the LAN interface in cleartext for nothing, and a DHCP change would have killed the relay silently (Finding 1 again). Now defaults to loopback and is `RC_VISION_UPLOAD_URL`-overridable, on the `core/game_host.py` "host is config, not code" principle - and the verifier confirmed the live `:8889` accepts the loopback POST (`{"ok": true, "size": 53}`) BEFORE the change was trusted, since getting this wrong would have broken the live relay. **19 tests as `tests/test_agent_relay_audit.py`; 4 mutations, all RED then restored byte-identical:** restore the literal in `screen_agent.py` -> 1 failed; restore it in the relay -> 2 failed; delete the `FileHandler` line -> 1 failed; revert the upload URL -> 1 failed. **THE LOGGING TEST TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS TO BECOME NON-VACUOUS, BY TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, AND ONLY MUTATION TESTING EVER SAID SO.** v1 inspected `logging.getLogger(...).handlers` from inside pytest and was reading PYTEST's own FileHandler - `logging.basicConfig` is a documented no-op when the root logger already has handlers, so the module's config never even applied; the mutation stayed green at 19 passed. v2 moved to a subprocess for a clean logging state but asserted a FIXED marker, and `logs/liveclient_relay.log` survives between runs, so the PREVIOUS run's line satisfied it - green a second time. v3 uses a per-run `uuid4` marker and finally goes RED; the verifier then tried to defeat it three ways (stale log present, two runs back to back, log moved aside) and could not. **VERIFIER GATE: CONFIRM on 6 of 7 claim groups, REFUTE on one - and the refuted one was a measurement error of mine that would have misdirected the next implementer.** I recorded that `screen_agent.py` and `phase_watcher.py` "already configure file logging" and were "the in-tree precedent to copy". They are not: both call `logging.basicConfig` with **no `filename=` and no `handlers=`** (`screen_agent.py:110`, `phase_watcher.py:129`), yielding a stderr-only StreamHandler that `pythonw` discards exactly like a print, and no `logs/screen_agent.log` or `logs/phase_watcher.log` exists. **My grep had counted the string `basicConfig` as evidence of file logging** - the function name, not the argument that matters. RM-154 was rewritten; it had been pointing at a broken template. **SEVEN DIMENSIONS.** CORRECTNESS **HARDENED** (the docstring's own warning is now true of the code). SECURITY **HARDENED** (Finding 2, plus a standing guard that scans every `_AGENT_ALLOWED` source file for 32-hex literals, so the next served file cannot quietly carry one). ERROR-HANDLING **HARDENED** (Finding 1; 401 given its own branch). RESOURCE-LIFETIME **CLEAN, expectation refuted** (both calls already bounded). INPUT-VALIDATION **N-A with a reason** - the relay is a pass-through by design and the shape gate is `vision_server/_http.py`, audited in cycle 2 (LEDGER 1177); adding a second validator here would duplicate it and could silently drop fields the coaches read. CONCURRENCY **CLEAN** (single-threaded poll loop, no shared state, no polled-file writes). MACHINE-ENV **HARDENED** (Finding 3, plus the `pythonw`/Last-Result reasoning behind `sys.exit(2)`). **TWO FINDINGS FILED, NOT FIXED.** **RM-154:** all THREE remaining agents lose their diagnostics under `pythonw` by two mechanisms (32 prints in `lcu_agent.py`; stderr-only basicConfig in the other two), and only the relay got the tokenless-exit guard, so the other three will now send an empty token and 401 silently - strictly better than sending a confidently WRONG one, but unfinished. **RM-155, found by accident and worth more than it cost:** the RC suite is **NOT IDEMPOTENT in a fresh tree**. `data/fusion_shadow.jsonl` is gitignored, so run 1 SKIPS `test_real_fusion_shadow_corpus_invariants` and passes 18133 - **and the suite itself writes one record to that production path during the run**. Run 2 then finds a 1-record corpus, no longer skips, and fails `assert narrowed > 0`. Measured end to end: deleted the file, ran the suite (18133 passed), confirmed the file was recreated with 1 record, then ran the single test and watched it fail. It never bites a developer box because the main tree's corpus holds 565 real records. **Explicitly NOT my regression** - the main tree at HEAD passes, and the same source passes in the worktree whenever the file is absent - and it is recorded here rather than quietly worked around because a suite that fails on its second consecutive run will otherwise be diagnosed as a phantom regression by whoever hits it next. **One self-inflicted failure, owned:** my first RM-154 draft pushed `ROADMAP.md` to 82834 bytes against its 81920 CI budget, which `test_doc_size_budget` caught; fixed by compressing RM-152 and RM-154 to tracker rows and leaving the narrative here, where it belongs. **Suites, observed THIS run from the repo root:** RC `tests/` **18133 passed / 154 skipped / 1635 subtests**, DS **10341 passed / 6462 subtests**, ruff `All checks passed!`, 0 non-ASCII added. **POST-DEPLOY ADDENDUM (same day, commit `05861539`) - the fix had a regression that only the deploy could reveal, and reading the deployed log is what caught it.** After restarting `RC-LiveClientRelay` onto the fixed code I read `logs/liveclient_relay.log` - the file the old code could never write - and it was emitting a WARNING every ~6 seconds. With no game running `:2999` is not listening, so every poll fails, and the new FileHandler faithfully recorded each one: roughly **2 MB/day of identical lines**, which would have buried the single line this whole audit exists to surface (the 401 from a stale token). **Giving a silent module an output channel is only half the job; the other half is not flooding it.** `fetch_live` now WARNs on a CHANGE of failure mode, DEBUGs while it repeats, and INFOs on recovery (which re-arms the warning) - the transition is the signal. 3 tests added, mutation-verified: removing the de-duplication turns 2 of them RED. **Measured live after redeploy:** the old process wrote ~50 warnings across 5 idle minutes; the new one logged the transition ONCE and then **0 lines of growth across 45 idle seconds**. This is the second cycle running where the real defect surfaced only from looking at deployed behaviour rather than at the diff (cycle 5's was the 3.33 GB nobody could see). **Don't-redo:** the relay's timeouts are already correct - do not "add" them; the hardcoded literal is DEAD and proven so by a live 401 - do not treat this as a credential-rotation incident; the same literal survives in 8 other TRACKED files that are NOT in `_AGENT_ALLOWED` and are therefore not published (noted in RM-154, out of scope); and do not copy `screen_agent.py` / `phase_watcher.py` as a logging template.

1182. DONE **2026-08-03 (lane 8 Headless-True-Audit cycle 5: `core/riot_api_cache.py` became a PERMANENT silent no-op if its DB file ever vanished, three docstring claims were untrue of the code, and the cache has quietly reached 3.33 GB; Tier-1).** Target chosen by criterion 1 (it persists external Riot API bodies), criterion 2 (it sits on the API-key path), criterion 3 (SQLite + WAL + threads) and criterion 4 (**zero** LEDGER mentions across 1181 entries - never audited). EXPECTATION recorded before reading: the API key leaking into a cache key or a log line, plus SQLite lifetime/threading issues. **THE HEADLINE EXPECTATION WAS REFUTED, AND THE DESIGN IT ATTACKED IS DELIBERATELY RIGHT** - recorded as a negative so the next audit does not re-spend on it. Cache keys carry `core/riot_api.py:125` `_key_fingerprint()`, which is genuinely `hashlib.sha256(key).hexdigest()[:12]` and not a truncation of the key; it exists for a real reason the docstring explains (PUUIDs are a per-API-key encryption of the same account, so a key rotation would otherwise poison immutable rows forever). The verifier went further than asked and scanned all 3.3 GB of `response_json`, not just the keys: **zero rows contain `RGAPI` in key OR payload**, and the live key file's own sha256[:12] (`1bfa0b180668`) is exactly the component appearing in the live keys, which proves the fingerprint is the thing being stored. **FINDING 1 - a vanished DB file killed the cache for the life of the process.** `_ensure_schema` short-circuits on `self._initialized`, which is PROCESS state, not FILE state. If the file goes away under a long-lived process (rotation, a cleanup pass, disk trouble), SQLite cheerfully recreates an EMPTY file on the next connect, the schema is never re-run, and every operation fails "no such table" - caught, logged at WARNING, returning None/False. **Callers cannot distinguish that from a cache miss**, so RC re-fetches from the Riot API on every single call, burning the rate limit, silently, until restart. Measured against the HEAD module before any edit: `set -> False`, `get -> None`, `_initialized` still True, and the verifier independently confirmed it stayed dead across five further attempts. `_heal_if_schema_vanished` now clears the flag on exactly that error, wired into all five soft-fail paths. **The limit is documented rather than oversold, and the verifier was asked to attack the honesty of that claim specifically:** the call that NOTICES still soft-fails (measured `False`), and only the SUBSEQUENT call heals. A same-call retry was considered and rejected - pretending a lost write succeeded would be worse than reporting it. **FINDING 2 - three claims untrue of the code.** The module docstring promised "a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction to avoid the dashboard request thread racing the priority-2 background scheduler"; the phrase occurred **exactly once in the file, inside that sentence**, and zero times in executable code. The CODE is fine - `isolation_level=None` autocommit plus single-statement `INSERT OR REPLACE` is atomic on its own, with writes further serialized by the instance lock - so the sentence was the defect, not the concurrency. Separately `purge_expired_ttl` claimed it was "called opportunistically by the rate-limit prune" and `stats` claimed it was "for the dashboard / metrics endpoint"; **neither caller exists**. Third consecutive cycle in which a module's own prose was the thing that was wrong. **NOT FIXED, FILED AS RM-153 - and it is the most operationally significant thing in this entry.** `cache_immutable` never expires BY DESIGN, and the live DB has reached **3,330,539,520 bytes across 12,305 rows** with `freelist_count = 0` and 3.32 GB of live payload - **all real data, so a VACUUM reclaims nothing** and this is genuine unbounded growth, not bloat. Nothing caps it, nothing evicts, nothing VACUUMs, and the only introspection - `stats()` - had no production callers AND reported ROW COUNTS only, so the one function that could have surfaced 3.3 GB was blind to the only dimension that mattered. `stats()` now also returns `immutable_bytes` and `db_file_bytes` (pre-existing keys preserved, verified against the fu02 suite's assertions on them); choosing an eviction policy is an operator call about RC's match corpus, not a lane-8 unilateral one, and RM-153 records the interaction to check first - `rewind_history.db` and the `.rofl` archive already retain match history separately, so some of the 3.3 GB may be duplicated retention rather than the only copy. **SEVEN DIMENSIONS.** CORRECTNESS **HARDENED** (three false claims corrected, all pinned by tests that read the source off disk). SECURITY **CLEAN, and proven rather than assumed** - the fingerprint design is correct, and the payload scan is the evidence. ERROR-HANDLING **HARDENED** (Finding 1 is the textbook silent-degradation case the audit charter names; the soft-fail contract itself is deliberate and preserved). RESOURCE-LIFETIME **CLEAN for connections** (every `_connect` is inside `try/finally: conn.close()`, and the assignment sits inside the outer `try` so a failed connect cannot NameError in the finally) but the DB FILE growth is the RM-153 tail. CONCURRENCY **CLEAN, exercised not trusted** - a 4-thread x 20-write test drives real contention and asserts 80 rows; the docstring's WAL/lock reasoning now matches the code. INPUT-VALIDATION **N/A** - keys and payloads are RC-authored here, and the untrusted-shape work belongs to `core/riot_api.py`, its caller. MACHINE-ENV **CLEAN**, with one trap recorded in RM-153: `journal_mode=WAL` means the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars are PART of the database, so any future archiver that copies the `.db` alone corrupts it (nothing does today - grepped). **11 tests as `tests/test_riot_api_cache_audit.py`; 5 mutations RED then restored byte-identical:** neuter the self-heal -> 3 failed; drop `immutable_bytes` -> 2; re-add the BEGIN IMMEDIATE promise -> 1; re-add the phantom-caller phrasing -> 1; re-add the phantom-consumer phrasing -> 1. Four tests survive all mutations and that is by design - two are declared positive controls, two cover other behaviour (concurrency, purge). **VERIFIER GATE: CONFIRM on all 8 claims, with 2 defects found in MY OWN WORK, both fixed before the commit.** (a) The new docstrings and RM-153 said `purge_expired_ttl`/`stats` have "NO callers anywhere in the tree" - **literally false**, `tests/fu02_team_context/test_riot_api_cache.py:96,104,112,129` calls both; corrected to "no PRODUCTION callers". (b) More seriously, the BEGIN IMMEDIATE guard computed its "is it in the code" half over everything after the module docstring, **including every method docstring**, so re-adding the false promise alongside a mere MENTION in any later docstring kept it GREEN - the verifier measured 11 passed on that evasion. **A guard that accepts prose as proof of code is precisely the `feedback_guard_on_nondefault_call_path_is_untested` shape**, and it was rebuilt to strip docstrings via `ast` before looking for the statement; the exact demonstrated evasion is now RED. **A mutation that silently failed to apply was caught and re-run rather than reported as passing:** the first attempt at the self-heal mutation used a shell heredoc that mangled the line-continuation backslash, the anchor assert fired, and the suite trivially passed 11 - re-done from a file-based script, which produced the real 3-test RED. **Suites, observed THIS run from the repo root:** RC `tests/` **18114 passed / 154 skipped / 1635 subtests**, DS **10341 passed / 6462 subtests**, `tests/fu02_team_context/` 111 passed, ruff `All checks passed!`, 0 non-ASCII bytes. **Don't-redo:** the `_key_fingerprint` design is CORRECT and measured - do not re-investigate it as a secret leak; the autocommit/no-explicit-transaction design is CORRECT - do not add a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` to satisfy a docstring that no longer claims one; the soft-fail-then-heal-next-call contract is DELIBERATE - do not convert it into a same-call retry without deciding that on purpose; and do not cite this entry as bounding the cache size, which is RM-153 and still open.

1181. DONE **2026-08-03 (lane 8 Headless-True-Audit cycle 4: `dashboard/api_schema.py` claimed to be an input gate and gates nothing, a negative `Content-Length` pinned a handler thread from the tailnet, and a non-dict body raised out of the route with NO response at all; Tier-1).** Target chosen by criterion 1 (the declared trust boundary for request bodies RC does not author) and criterion 4 (load-bearing, **zero** LEDGER mentions in 1180 entries, no dedicated test module). EXPECTATION recorded before reading: `_AllowExtra` where `_ForbidExtra` belongs, and missing range/length bounds. **One half was right, one half was REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT and is recorded as a negative:** the `items: list[str] = []` / `coach: dict = {}` field defaults look exactly like the classic shared-mutable-default bug and are NOT one - pydantic v2 deep-copies defaults per instance, proven by constructing two models and mutating them independently. That is the dataclass intuition being wrong, and it is pinned by a test so the next auditor does not re-spend on it. **FINDING 1 - the module's central claim was false in two independent ways.** `api_schema.py:5` read "POST body models use extra=forbid (strict input gates)". Measured against `_dispatch._REQUEST_MODELS`: **4 of the 6 wired POST paths use `extra="allow"`** (ds-preview, build-order, speak, team-context/refresh), so the policy is not uniform. And none of the six is a GATE at all - `_dispatch._validate_request_body` logs a WARNING per field error and **never raises**, after which `dispatch_post` calls the route with the unchanged body regardless. The models are a logging decoration. The soft-warn design is DELIBERATE and documented at the dispatcher; the defect is that the schema module advertised something else, which invites the next route author to skip their own validation on the strength of a gate that does not exist. Rewritten to state what the layer actually does, with the per-path census and the soft contract both pinned by tests. **FINDING 2 - a negative `Content-Length` read to EOF.** `do_POST` caps the body with `if n > _MAX_POST_BYTES`, but `int("-1")` is -1, which passes that check, and `self.rfile.read(n) if n else b""` then treats -1 as truthy. Measured against the real `Handler` on an ephemeral port, and the discriminator is what makes it a hang rather than a crash: the request returned NOTHING for 4.01s, then completed **0.13s after the client shut down its write side** - the read-to-EOF signature. `dashboard/server.py:35` binds `HOST = "::"` and `:54` is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`, so the cost is one pinned thread per request from anywhere on the LAN or tailnet; the verifier added the sharpening detail that the body read at `_handler.py:314-332` runs **BEFORE** the `RC_DASH_TOKEN` check at `:342`, so even a configured token would not gate it (and `RC_DASH_TOKEN` is unset in this deployment anyway - confirmed live, an unauthenticated `/api/command` returns 400 not 401). **This is the SAME defect closed in `vision_server/_http.py` earlier the same day (LEDGER 1177), and 1177's sweep never looked across files** - so the wider of the two surfaces kept it for the rest of the day. **CROSS-FILE SWEEP, done properly this time:** every `Content-Length` reader in the tree was enumerated and re-checked independently by the verifier. `agents/_supervisor_http.py:114` (`length <= 0 or > 256 KiB`), `agents/daemon_slayer/server.py:2698` (`while remaining > 0`) and `:2706` (`if length <= 0`), and `mc/handler.py:117` (an explicit negative check, already carrying a comment describing this exact bug) are all SAFE. **`tools/ds_matchdb_mcp_server.py:657` had it** - fixed in the same slice; severity is genuinely lower there (loopback `127.0.0.1:8861` and `_check_auth` runs before the read) and that is stated rather than inflated. **FINDING 3 - the one this audit got WRONG, corrected by the gate.** The first draft of this work claimed "the routes defend themselves, so nothing is currently exploitable because of Finding 1", citing `_serve_command_post`'s command whitelist. **The verifier REFUTED it, and the counterexample was the very route cited as the defence:** the whitelist checks the command STRING, but nothing checked the body was a dict, so `POST /api/command` with `[1,2,3]` raised an **uncaught `AttributeError` at `routes_state.py:516`, dumping a traceback to stderr and closing the connection with NO HTTP RESPONSE AT ALL**. `/api/input` behaved identically at `:503`; ds-preview, build-order and speak degraded to 500; only `/api/team-context/refresh` actually checked. The irony is exact: `_validate_request_body` ALREADY notices this case ("expected dict, got list") and then returns without acting, because it is soft by design. Fixed once at the trust boundary in `do_POST` (dict-or-400) rather than in ~40 route handlers, after first verifying by AST-style scan that **zero** POST routes consume a positional or list body, so the narrowing costs nothing. Same root-cause family as 1180 - a payload shape assumed rather than asserted - which is now the third consecutive cycle to find that family. **14 tests added as `tests/test_dashboard_post_trust_boundary.py`, driving the real handlers over real sockets; 5 mutations, all RED then restored byte-identical:** drop the `n < 0` guard -> 1 failed; restore "strict input gates" -> 1; flip `SpeakRequest` to `_ForbidExtra` -> 1 (proving the census pin is live, not decorative); drop the MCP `n < 0` guard -> 1; drop the non-dict guard -> **4** failed. Four of the fourteen are declared positive controls (normal body, empty body, oversize still 413, defaults-are-isolated) and survive every mutation by design. The verifier also caught that the contract test used a relative `Path("dashboard/api_schema.py")` and so silently depended on CWD - re-anchored on `dashboard.api_schema.__file__`. **SEVEN DIMENSIONS.** CORRECTNESS **HARDENED** (the module docstring was false; now pinned by a test that reads the contract off disk). SECURITY **HARDENED** (findings 2 and 3). INPUT-VALIDATION **HARDENED** (dict-or-400 at the boundary). ERROR-HANDLING **HARDENED** (an uncaught exception with no response is the worst case of the class; note the CLAUDE.md raw-error rule is satisfied - `do_POST` deliberately does not echo the exception text, per its 2026-04-27 comment). RESOURCE-LIFETIME **PARTIALLY HARDENED, and explicitly NOT closed - see below**. CONCURRENCY **CLEAN** (no polled-file writes here; `ThreadingHTTPServer` per-connection isolation is the existing design). MACHINE-ENV **HARDENED** (the `::` bind plus pre-auth body read is what turns a parsing bug into a remote thread-pin, and is now recorded). **THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ENTRY, because an unqualified claim here would be false: THIS DOES NOT MAKE THE DASHBOARD SLOWLORIS-SAFE.** The verifier measured it against the FIXED handler: a perfectly legal `Content-Length: 1048575`, under the cap, with zero body sent, produces no response for 4.01s and releases 0.18s after SHUT_WR - **identical pinned thread, still unauthenticated, still reachable from `::`**. The fix removes one TRIGGER, not the vulnerability. The real fix is a connection read timeout, which is a behaviour change for every dashboard client including the 500 ms `/api/state` poll and `_proxy_to_supervisor`, which STREAMS an upstream response and could be truncated by a naive deadline - a deliberate design change, not a hardening tweak. Filed as **RM-152** with the acceptance criteria, alongside two non-production residuals the sweep found and deliberately left: `tests/snapshot_panels/conftest.py:98-100` (test fixture) and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-mission-control-s10-decouple.md:700`, which carries the vulnerable line **in an unimplemented spec** - fix it there or it ships the bug a fourth time. **BACKFILL (6e):** nothing to repair. All three defects are request-scoped and write no state - the negative-CL hang pins a thread and releases it when the client goes away, and the non-dict crash aborts before any route side effect. The already-bad state that DID exist is a running process on vulnerable code, which is the other half of 6e and IS addressed: RC restarted and re-probed, and `RC-DS-MatchDB-MCP` bounced SEPARATELY because - per LEDGER 1179 - `restart_trigger.txt` does not redeploy anything that is not the RC process. **Suites, observed THIS run from the repo root:** RC `tests/` **18103 passed / 154 skipped / 1635 subtests**, DS **10341 passed / 6462 subtests**, ruff `All checks passed!`, 0 non-ASCII bytes added. **Verifier gate: CONFIRM on claims 1, 2, 3, 6, 7; REFUTE on 4 (the "nothing is exploitable" overclaim, which became Finding 3 and a real fix) and REFUTE on a count (I said 10 tests, there were 9 at that point).** Third cycle running in which the adversarial pass found something in the WRITE-UP rather than the diff - but the first in which it found a genuine CODE hole by attacking a limiting claim, which is the strongest argument yet for attacking the sentences that make a finding sound smaller. **Don't-redo:** the pydantic mutable defaults are FINE (measured, pinned); the soft-warn dispatcher is DELIBERATE - do not "fix" it into a strict gate without deciding that on purpose, the test pins it precisely so that change is conscious; and do not cite this entry as closing the thread-pin DoS, which is RM-152 and still open.

The shape half was worse than expected, and the real headline was not a shape bug at all but the ASYMMETRY that made it fatal. **WEAKNESS 1, MEASURED BEFORE A LINE WAS CHANGED.** `_save_eog` builds its team-comp map at the top of the function, OUTSIDE the `try` that guards the database block, and called `team.get(...)` / `p.get(...)` with no shape check. Measured on the real loop with a stubbed raising capture: the thread was **dead after the first trigger**, and a second `trigger()` never reached `_capture_after_trigger` at all - `capture calls = 1` across both. **SIBLING SWEEP, per the root-cause-fix rule, found the same class three more times in the same file:** `_adapt_match_history` iterated `participants`, `participantIdentities` and `teams` with the same bare `.get`, plus a `pinfo = ident.get("player") or {}` that still raised on a TRUTHY non-dict. There the exception was CONTAINED (the caller wraps it) but it discarded the entire history fallback for one bad member and logged at DEBUG only - the quieter half of the same defect, and exactly the silent-no-op family item 965 closed twice in this file already. Fixed with `_as_list` plus per-entry `isinstance` filters so a wrong-shape entry costs that ENTRY, never the match. **9 tests added as `tests/test_lcu_postgame_collector_audit.py`; 5 mutations, all RED then restored green:** revert `_dict_players` to the raw list -> 2 failed; delete the `teams` isinstance filter -> 1; delete the `_run` try -> 1; revert the three `_adapt_match_history` comprehensions -> 2; revert `pinfo` -> 1. DONE **2026-08-03 (stop-claim gate: a file CITED as a precedent is not an edit claim, and a NEGATED claim is not a claim; Tier-1).** Second and third members of the same family as item 1175, both measured the same day on the lane-8 session, both with the identical unrecoverable property: `tools/stop_claim_gate.py` scans the TRANSCRIPT, so a sentence already emitted cannot be retracted and one false positive blocks every subsequent Stop for the life of the session. **(a) `file_claim_without_edit` on a CITATION.** `CLAIM_FILE` matches a claim-verb within 40 chars of a filename and cannot tell "fixed X" from "fixed it the way X does". The blocking sentence was "Fixed with the in-tree precedent at `dashboard/routes_static.py:64-67`" - naming the file the fix was COPIED FROM, on a session that never touched it. The incentive this creates is the damning part and is why it was fixed rather than worked around: **the cheapest way to satisfy the gate is to stop citing precedent**, and citing precedent is exactly the behaviour the repo wants (the same commit's sibling entry 1177 exists BECAUSE the fix reused an existing pattern instead of inventing one). Discriminator = a citation marker (`precedent|per|see|cited|as in|example|documented|following|reference|pattern at/in/from`) occurring BETWEEN the claim verb and the path - that POSITION is what puts the path in a citation role - vetoed by the existing `CLAIM_FIRST_PERSON_DID`, so "I fixed it per the precedent in `routes_static.py`" still flags. A marker AFTER the path does not suppress, so a trailing "per the precedent" cannot retro-license a real claim. Required switching the loop from `findall` to `finditer`, since only the match SPAN can locate "between". **(b) `commit_claim_without_commit` on a NEGATION.** "Nothing is committed yet" asserts the OPPOSITE of having committed, and reporting honestly that nothing had been committed was itself flagged as an unbacked commit claim - the gate punishing accurate self-reporting. Discriminator = a negation in the 40 chars immediately BEFORE the matched claim word, so the negation must GOVERN it: "I committed the fix, but not the docs" still flags. Applied to `CLAIM_PUSH` in the same commit rather than one at a time, per the root-cause-plus-siblings rule - the identical "nothing is pushed yet" would have bitten the next session. **9 tests added (62 passed total), and MUTATION-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS because a suppression is precisely the change that can silently become an evasion hatch:** remove the citation suppression -> 3 RED (non-vacuous); remove the first-person veto -> 3 RED (the veto is load-bearing); remove the commit negation guard -> 1 RED; widen the negation scope from 40 chars to the whole sentence -> 2 RED (the scoping is load-bearing, not decoration). **One of those tests was VACUOUS as first written and only mutation testing caught it** - the three veto cases put the citation marker AFTER the path, where the suppression never fires at all, so they passed with the veto deleted and proved nothing; rewritten with the marker in the lead position, and the case is now a marker-identical contrast pair with its first-person-free twin. Textbook `feedback_guard_on_nondefault_call_path_is_untested`. **Verified END-TO-END on the real input, per the 1175 precedent:** the fixed gate run against this session's own live transcript returns **0 findings, exit 0**, where the shipped gate returned 3 and blocked. **KNOWN AND DELIBERATE: this does NOT unblock the session that found it.** The Stop hook executes `C:\Riot Commander\tools\stop_claim_gate.py` - the MAIN TREE's copy - while the repair is on `lane/true-audit`, which is the same shared-hook trap the lane-8 skill documents for `core.hooksPath`. Editing the main tree from a lane worktree to silence a gate would have been strictly worse than wearing the false positive, so the block was reported and left standing. It clears on merge.

Then I "corrected" that with a second wrong claim - that `moon_proxy` was the capture path and the row's precondition tested the wrong endpoint - inferred from a log line reading `Vision via Moon-PC (moon_proxy)`. **`moon_proxy` is the MODEL TRANSPORT, not a capture source**: `extract_vision(img_b64, ...)` takes an image it is handed, and `shared_vision.py:278/310` still sources that image from `_capture_screen()` -> `/latest-frame`. Only READING `_capture_screen` settled it, and reading it is also what exposed the token requirement. A log line naming a component is not evidence about which component OWNS the step. **RM-148 INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED in the same pass and upgraded from plausible to confirmed** (corroboration appended to `BACKLOG.md`, not re-filed): my new suite reported `5 passed, 1 error` on `data/vision_state.json`, deselecting the only network-calling test STILL fired the guard, and the flagged test passes 1/1 alone. New tells recorded: the mutated file set differs run to run, and the false positive is DURATION-SENSITIVE (0.25s clean, 1.4s and 1.9s both fire), so it scales with suite runtime. The conclusion rests on the in-game means and the committed-memory delta, both captured pre-restart on one process - the watcher's guard did its job and I did not substitute the missing sample with a guess. (2) A ~+1.2 MB/min in-game drift exists but is NOT separable from the 500-548 oscillation over one match; it is explicitly not a finding. **The restart-loop guard was correct throughout and was never touched** - the filing's own instruction on that held up. **Don't-redo:** do not walk 700/1200 back without re-measuring; do not treat 105 MB as "the" from-boot baseline; do not attribute the 810 MB peak to resolution flips; do not report the +1.2 MB/min slope as a leak; do not edit `core/resource_manager.py` mid-measurement, it hot-reloads and invalidates a same-process test.

A garbage or absent side counts as CHANGED so one apply runs and the snapshot self-heals; the alternative (no-op on garbage) reproduces the very symptom being fixed. The wiring half re-runs the SAME `resolveOverlayMetrics({workArea: primary.bounds, scaleFactor})` create time runs, coalesced on a 600ms settle because Windows emits a burst during a mode switch and mid-switch Electron can still report the OUTGOING geometry - so the re-apply rides the LAST event, not the first. **Item 567's source choice is preserved and now pinned:** `primary.bounds`, never the taskbar-excluded work area, because work-area sizing makes ovscale 1.296 instead of 1.333 and lands every design-px widget about 3 percent off the game minimap. A test asserts the re-apply function body contains `workArea: primary.bounds` and does NOT contain `primary.workArea`, so a future edit cannot fix the tracking by quietly breaking the alignment. 13 tests, red first, ruff/ASCII clean, full rc-shell suite 339 green. **THE NEW TEST FILE HAD TO BE ADDED TO `rc-shell/package.json`** - the `test` script enumerates every file by name and nothing globs the directory, so a new `test/*.test.js` runs only when invoked by hand and is invisible to the suite otherwise. **Mutation-checked rather than assumed:** deleting the `watchDisplayChanges()` call from `app.whenReady` turns the wiring test red (verified by mutating the file and restoring it, not by `git checkout`, which would have taken the unstaged work with it). **NOT CLOSED, and the reason is the point:** the re-apply is gated on an overlay WINDOW existing, and that window is created lazily on first in-game show, so with no game up `applyOverlayDisplayMetrics` early-returns and a headless resolution flip proves exactly nothing. Claiming the fix live off the pure function returning `{reload:true}` would be textbook SUBSTITUTION - the failure class that killed most of the 2026-07-18 synthetic-drain attempt. Filed as `docs/LIVE_GAME_GATED_SYNC.md` **G6-04** with the receipt named: the overlay's own access-log request line carries the computed value (`GET /?overlay=1&panelset=...&ovscale=N`), so two entries with DIFFERENT `ovscale` around a flip and a flip-back is the evidence, and it must be tested in BOTH directions because the return trip is the half that was broken. Requires G6-01 (rc-shell MAIN relaunched on this code) first - the renderer auto-reloads via ADR-008, MAIN does not. **Don't-redo:** do not substitute `primary.workArea` for `primary.bounds` in the re-apply; do not collapse `reposition`/`reload` into one flag; do not add a new `rc-shell/test/*.test.js` without adding it to the package.json `test` script.

DONE **2026-08-01 (RM-136 fourth false positive - the armed gate blocked a wrap whose CI claim was backed by a dozen probes, because BOTH of the transports used were invisible to it).** Tier-1, one tool + its tests. **The claim was TRUE: `gh run list` / `gh run view` ran repeatedly this session and returned `completed success`, and the gate still reported `ci_claim_without_probe`.** Two distinct transports, one root cause. **(1) `&&` cuts the span.** `EV_CI` is `\bgh(?:\.exe)?\b[^|&\n]*?\b(?:run|pr|api|workflow)\b` - deliberately `&`-terminated so a pipeline cannot borrow the match - so the class-3 fix only ever reached the SEMICOLON form (`GH="..."; "$GH" run list`). The `&&` form the done ritual actually produces (`cd X && GH="..." && "$GH" run list`) has an `&` between the binding and the subcommand and never matched. **(2) The far worse one: a `python -c "<script>"` probe is ENTIRELY inside one quoted literal, and `strip_command_noise` deletes quoted literals as DATA, so after stripping the command reads `python -c` and NOTHING is left. No pattern over the stripped text could ever have seen it.** That is the important finding - the third fix (LEDGER 1156) tuned a regex when part of the problem was that the evidence had already been thrown away upstream of every regex. **Also worth recording against the class-3 entry: its docstring overstates what it built.** `EV_CI` matches the class-3 shape only because `\bgh\b` is case-insensitive and hits the VARIABLE NAME `GH` in the surviving `GH= ; run list`, not a binary at all. It works, and it is looser than its own comment claims. **Fix: `EV_CI_VAR`, evaluated on the pre-quote-strip text, binding the SAME NAME** - capture the identifier assigned a gh binary path, then require that identifier (back-referenced) immediately ahead of a gh subcommand. Heredocs ARE still stripped for it, so writing the recipe into a doc stays documentation. **The rejected alternative matters as much as the chosen one: widening `EV_CI`'s span to allow `&` and `\n` would credit ANY later `run` after ANY `gh` mention, which is precisely the looseness that produced the first armed session's 9 false positives.** Three load-bearing NEGATIVES, all written to fail first: an assignment never invoked is setup and not evidence; a DIFFERENT variable in front of `run` cannot borrow the gh binding (this is why the name is captured and back-referenced rather than matched loosely); and a heredoc that documents the invocation is not a probe. **Both new code paths mutation-proven:** disabling `EV_CI_VAR` fails 1, removing the heredoc strip from its input fails 1, file restored byte-identical (verified). Suite 42 -> **47 passed**. **END-TO-END, not a fixture claim: this session's own transcript - the one that produced the block - replays through the fixed gate to `findings 0, rc 0`.** Gate STAYS ARMED; must-not-fire negatives 10 -> 13. Full `tests/` 17836 passed / 108 skipped / 0 failed, drift_guard 0 breaches. ENGINE-IMPACT NONE.

DONE **2026-08-01 (RM-136 - the ARMED gate blocked a Stop on a claim that WAS backed; two false-positive classes found by replaying the session's own transcript, both fixed by narrowing, neither by loosening).** Tier-1: the gate plus its tests. **THE GATE WAS WRONG AND THE CLAIM WAS TRUE, which is the exact failure mode that gets a gate disabled forever - so it is worth more than the two-line diff suggests.** It fired on `17784 passed` with `observed '26, 29, 30, 52'`. **CLASS 1 - A BACKGROUNDED RUN DEFERS ITS SUMMARY, AND THE EVIDENCE COLLECTOR WAS BLIND TO THAT TRANSPORT.** `collect_evidence` pairs a pytest `tool_use` with the `tool_result` that follows it, but a run started with `run_in_background` answers with a LAUNCHER HANDOFF (`Command running in background with ID: ...`), not a summary. The real summary lands later, when the output file is read by some unrelated `tail`, whose command does not match `EV_PYTEST` and is therefore never collected. So every foreground count (26/29/30/52) was observed and the one number that mattered was not. This is `reference_ds_route_seam_transport_vs_flag` in a new place: the check was correct, settable and green, and the TRANSPORT was missing. Fix: detect the handoff, hold the run OPEN, and attach the first later `tool_result` carrying a pytest TERMINAL-SUMMARY line to that run. **The tightness is the whole design** - crediting a bare `N passed` floating anywhere is precisely what produced the first armed session's 9 false positives, so `EV_SUMMARY_LINE` requires the trailing duration (`... in 170.67s`) and the credit is attached to a specific deferred run rather than free-floating. Two negatives are load-bearing and were written to fail first: a non-summary `99999 passed` mention after a background run stays UNcredited, and with NO background run a summary-shaped string in an unrelated tool result never becomes evidence. **CLASS 2 - PROSE ORDINALS READ AS SUITE COUNTS.** The replay's last survivor was `Test 1 passed for the wrong reason`, flagged as a claim of a 1-test suite. "Test 1 passed" names ONE case; "1397 passed" counts a suite; same three tokens, opposite meanings. `re` has no variable-width lookbehind, so `CLAIM_COUNT` now captures the preceding word and `CLAIM_COUNT_ORDINAL` filters 16 of them (test / case / step / mutant / round / ...). Guarded by a positive: `The suite reports 1500 passed` against a 1397 run must STILL flag. **A TEST I WROTE PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON AND I CAUGHT IT ONLY BY CHECKING WHICH TESTS WENT RED.** The first deferred-summary fixture had no foreground run, so `observed_counts` was EMPTY, and check 2 short-circuits on `if observed_counts and ...` - the fixture could never flag whatever the claim said. It passed BEFORE the fix. The measured session had small foreground runs filling that set, and that is what made the big deferred number read as unobserved; the fixture now carries a leading `30 passed` run and the reason is written into its docstring. Same family as `feedback_parallel_slice_stubs_and_vacuous_regression_tests`: green is not evidence, RED-THEN-GREEN is. **Both fixes mutation-proven:** `elif False` on the deferred-credit branch fails 2, `if False` on the ordinal filter fails 3, 0 residue after restore. **END-TO-END PROOF, not a fixture claim: this session's own transcript - the one that produced the block - replays through the fixed gate to `findings 0, rc 0`.** **CLASS 3, found the same way one wrap later: `gh` INVOKED BY ABSOLUTE PATH THROUGH A VARIABLE.** `EV_CI` required the binary ADJACENT to its subcommand (`gh run`), but `docs/OPERATIONS.md` and the done ritual both mandate the absolute path - `GH="C:/Program Files/GitHub CLI/gh.exe"; "$GH" run list` - so the literal `gh run` never appears and a real, repeated CI probe read as NO probe. **The gate's own house style guaranteed this fires on every single wrap**, which is how a gate gets disabled. The binary and subcommand may now be separated within one command segment, with the span stopping at `|` and `&` so a pipeline cannot borrow the match. Two negatives hold it honest: a CI claim with NO gh probe anywhere still flags, and a bare `run` word without a gh binary proves nothing. Mutation-proven - restoring the old adjacency regex fails the new test. Session transcript replays to `findings 0` a second time. Suite 30 -> 38 -> **42 passed**. **All three classes are the same defect wearing different clothes: the gate read the RIGHT evidence in the WRONG PLACE - a deferred transport, a prose ordinal, an aliased binary - and in none of them was the CHECK wrong.** That is why every fix here narrows a PARSER and none touches a check. The gate STAYS ARMED; its negatives-that-must-not-fire grew from 2 to 10. ENGINE-IMPACT NONE.

The `-n`-only failure now fails in ANY run, at the call site, naming the offending kwarg and prescribing the fix. Repo-ROOT because `tests/conftest.py` cannot reach `agents/daemon_slayer/tests/`, which has no conftest of its own and had one of the five instances. **DEFECT-CLASS ENUMERATION, MECHANIZED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** The probe is the guard itself: install it, run the full dual suite, and every one of the 463 pre-existing call sites reports. Result **23861 passed, 106 skipped, 6178 subtests, 0 failed** - exactly +12 tests and +17 subtests over the pre-change baseline, which is my new file to the unit, and therefore **0 additional instances repo-wide.** Full disposition: 5 historical instances FIXED (`cd0f115d`), 458 remaining sites CLEAN and now machine-proven rather than eye-proven, 0 OUT-OF-SCOPE. **cd0f115d's sweep was CORRECT** - this is a case where the by-eye claim held up, and the value delivered is that it is no longer a claim. **A MEASURED-WRONG FACT IN A COMMITTED DOCSTRING, CAUGHT BY BUILDING THE PROBE.** `tests/test_aram_action_rule.py` asserted that a bare `object()` "(or a `set()`)" raises DumpError. Probed against execnet directly: `set` and `frozenset` serialize FINE; the containers recurse, so `[object()]` fails while `{1, 2}` does not. The wrong half was never load-bearing - no test passed a set - but it was the kind of remembered-not-measured detail that sends the next reader rewriting working code. Corrected, and the grammar is now PINNED by a test (`ChannelSafetyGrammarTests`) instead of restated from memory in a docstring. **A docstring is not a gate; if a fact matters enough to write down twice, assert it.** **KNOWN REACH LIMIT, RECORDED NOT PAPERED OVER.** The verifier caught that a rootdir conftest is only loaded when pytest is invoked from the repo root, so running the DS suite from inside `agents/daemon_slayer/` bypasses the guard. NOT closed with a second conftest under `agents/daemon_slayer/tests/`, because that path is mirrored into `Share/src/` and `Share/` runs its suite standalone (RM-112) where `tests._subtest_channel_guard` does not exist - the mirror would import a missing module and break a package that is currently clean. The gap is already fenced by an unrelated standing rule (a DS-dir invocation produces 13 CWD failures - [[reference_ds_suite_run_from_repo_root]]) and CI runs from the root. Written into the module docstring so the next reader does not "fix" it into a Share breakage. **Verifier subagent CONFIRM 6/6**, including the load-bearing one I could not self-certify: it wrote a throwaway `subTest(bad=object())` test INTO the DS suite, confirmed it fails with the guard's TypeError raised from `_subtest_channel_guard.py:82`, then deleted it and proved no residue - so the guard demonstrably reaches the suite that has no conftest, rather than merely being importable. It also corrected my arithmetic (`cd0f115d` fixed 5 subTest sites; the 6 in `--stat` is the FILE count) and independently byte-scanned all four touched files (0 bytes >= 0x80). Gate: full dual suite **23861 passed / 106 skipped / 6178 subtests / 0 failed** under `-n 8`; hygiene trio 14 passed; `ruff check .` clean; `py_compile` clean; drift_guard 1 breach, PRE-EXISTING and reported not silenced - `ROADMAP.md` is at 91% of its 81920-byte budget and was already breaching at HEAD (73178 bytes before this session), so the ROADMAP edit was deliberately compressed with the detail carried here instead, which is where CLAUDE.md says per-item detail belongs. **THE LESSON: an executor-override that hunts for drift BETWEEN a digest and a file cannot see drift in the file itself, and a queue row is a claim with a timestamp, not a fact.** The cheapest possible check - run the thing the row says is broken, before fixing it - cost 132 seconds and turned a fix-6-failures cycle into a gate the repo did not have. **CARRY-FORWARD (unchanged, still unclaimed): the 16-instance whole-file-rewrite-under-a-narrowed-work-plan class from LEDGER 1092 has a live DS-consumer blast radius and should be scheduled before someone runs a narrowed regen by hand.** RM-121 item 3 is now COMPLETE; next is item 4, `random.txt` + `roadmap work.txt`. **POST-COMMIT: THE PUSH TURNED `docs-guards` RED, AND THE CAUSE WAS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN THIS DIFF.** `test_real_orchestration_plan_newest_row_survives` failed because the loop director reads `docs/ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md` through `cap_bytes_head_tail(..., PLAN_CTX_CAP=24000, PLAN_CTX_HEAD=8000)` - first 8000 bytes plus the LAST 16000 - and R216's row landed **16087 bytes from EOF, missing the tail window by 87 bytes.** Arithmetic, not luck: every cycle appends a ROW in the middle and a FINDINGS block at the END, so the newest row is pushed about one findings-block further from EOF each cycle while barely moving itself (R215 sat near 13500, R216 at 16087, R217 would have been near 20000). **It was going to fail every cycle from here** - it merely broke on the cycle whose entire subject is gates that fire too late to matter. 956. DONE **2026-07-19 (RM-98 ADJUDICATED - the cast-rate time base is a documented-but-unadjudicated INHERITANCE, the "haste-inclusive" defence is RETRACTED, and both fixes RM-39 named are INFEASIBLE).** Tier-0, docs only, ENGINE stays 1.223.0. Item 955 filed RM-98 as **SIZED, NOT ADJUDICATED** with one open question: is the whole-game basis of `data/daemon_slayer/spell_cast_rates.json` a deliberate modelling choice or an accident of reusing a convenient table? **VERDICT: neither.** Exactly one denominator-adjacent choice was ever made deliberately and recorded, and it was **measured vs `1/cooldown`**, not whole-game vs combat-window (`docs/history_notes.md:12534`: "Veigar Q has 4s base cooldown -> theoretical 0.25 casts/sec; measured median is 0.098"). That choice is defensible and stands. The DENOMINATOR was never in the option set - a combat-window basis appears nowhere in the generator, in commit `34e1d6c2`, or in any s178-era doc, and its first appearance anywhere in the repo is 2026-07 in `docs/specs/RM39_design_C_baseline_delta.md:416-421` as an audit finding. The basis was inherited by SHAPE, and the generator admits it (`scripts/build_spell_cast_rates.py:9-11`): "Mirror of the (undocumented) s145 ad-hoc query that built `ult_cast_rates.json` for the Malignance Hatefog proc". **The "locally correct at origin" defence also fails:** the s145 ancestor was ALREADY multiplying a whole-game rate into a per-second combat term (`ult_rates.py:5-7` describes it as converting "ult cast frequency into a DPS-time proc rate"), so there is no point in the chain where whole-game was adjudicated correct for a DPS context. Nothing would have caught a base swap - `test_cast_rates.py:194-197` asserts only `0.01 < rate < 1.0`, a 100x-wide band that passes under either basis. **THE STATED BLOCKER IS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED.** RM-98's filing defended the basis as "haste-inclusive by construction, which is why the RM-39/RM-43 haste adjudication relied on it". Both halves are wrong. Haste-inclusiveness follows from the table being **MEASURED**, not from the denominator - a combat-window empirical table is equally an observation of a population that already built whatever haste it built, and the generator attributes it correctly at `build_spell_cast_rates.py:5-7` ("a **measured** cast rate already encodes mana/cooldown downtime"). And RM-39 did not rely on the whole-game basis, it **condemned** it: `SPEC_rm39_rm43_ability_haste.md:187-192` calls the OPPOSITE argument decisive ("a statistic too diluted to SHOW haste is equally too diluted to have EMBEDDED the population-haste bias"), and `:174-176` / `:198-202` / `:318-320` prescribe REPLACING the denominator ("If the denominator is wrong, the fix is a better denominator, not a correction factor layered on top"). RM-39's verdict rests on disqualifiers 1.1 and 1.3 (call signature, call counting), neither whole-game dependent - per `e382d9c4`, "it rests on code structure and call-counting". **The false claim entered by SUMMARISATION, and the mechanism is the transferable lesson:** three artifacts (`project_ds_ability_haste_measured_inert`, `docs/LEDGER.md:51`, `WAKEUP_NOTES.md:130`) each weld "whole-game duration" and "already haste-inclusive" into a single clause with an "and"; a later summary read the conjunction as CAUSATION and manufactured a blocker out of it. Two true facts joined by "and" became a false "because". **FOUR CORRECTIONS TO RM-98 AS FILED:** (1) **the defect ALREADY SHIPS DEFAULT-ON in three scorers** - the identical plain sum is live in `ds.onhit` (`onhit_dps.py:143`, Slice B 2026-07-16, routed at `server.py:2107` `/rank-onhit`, confirmed live-serving), `ds.dps` (`dps.py:1023`, Malignance) and `ds.hps` (`hps.py:679`), so gating a DEFAULT-OFF flag on a defect three shipped scorers already carry is incoherent; **two docstrings assert the falsehood outright** - `onhit_dps.py:4-5` ("into ONE combined-DPS score by PLAIN SUM - both halves are in the same DPS units") and `hybrid.py:151-153`, which names the very step that BREAKS additivity as its reason for additivity ("Rows are already post-mitigation and post-cast-rate ..., so the sum is directly additive"). (2) **The term is NOT inert.** This was hypothesised at session start and REFUTED by measurement: per-cast damage is an order of magnitude larger than per-second auto damage (Renekton W is 226.25 dmg/cast against a `weighted_dps` of 29.14 dmg/s, so 0.0184 casts/s still yields 4.17 DPS), the ability term is **30.5%** of Renekton's ON damage term, **29.2% cohort mean**, **65.9% for Riven**, and it demonstrably re-orders (max `|delta delta_pct|` 0.286 over top-20). It survives the ratio sort because it is additive and item-dependent (`delta_A/delta_W` spans 0.000 Dead Man's Plate to 0.430 Black Cleaver). Scaling it 27x would not correct a small term, it would INVERT the scorer - the ability term becomes 92% of the denominator and Trinity Force falls out of the top 20. (3) **27x overstates.** Per-spell against the rotation-implied reference: Q **7.83x**, W **27.12x**, E **6.44x** - characteristic distortion ~7x, W is the outlier. And the 0.5/s reference is `w: 1.5 / duration: 3` from `scenarios.json`, a field `_rotation_attack_dps` **never reads** (`dps.py:549-566` reads only `duration`, `basic`, `basicTime`, `numberOfTargets`). The 27x is a dimensional-error illustration, NOT two live engine values disagreeing. (4) **Under-scoped** - as filed it covers `hybrid.py:595` only, missing `ability_dps.py:1252` where **6 champions (Aphelios, Katarina, Kled, Teemo, Vayne, Vi) sum a `1/cooldown` COMBAT basis and the whole-game MEASURED basis inside ONE total**, plus the always-on `item_proc_dps` fold (27.9% of Veigar's total) and the three consumers above. **BOTH FIXES RM-39 NAMED ARE INFEASIBLE - and the spec explicitly said nobody had sized them** (`SPEC:198-202`, "A, C and D independently converged on this and none of them sized it"). Sized here against `data/rewind_history.db`: **"casts per second alive"** is directly computable (`participants.time_spent_dead` exists) but lifts Renekton W only from 0.02351 to 0.02927, a **1.25x** correction against a 27x gap with 17.1x remaining (130 matches, dead fraction median 0.204) - so the gap is overwhelmingly LANING and non-combat time, not death timers, and this candidate is INADEQUATE. **"per second within N seconds of damage dealt or taken"** requires sub-window resolution, but `timeline_frames` carries 685,364 rows at a **60-second cadence** (measured deltas 60016-60021 ms); a 3-10s combat window is not resolvable from 1-minute buckets, and the best achievable derivative is "minutes in which any combat occurred" - NOT AVAILABLE at the required fidelity. **RECOMMENDATION: do not chase a denominator replacement.** The data cannot support one and a correction factor is explicitly ruled out by RM-39. Take the other half of `SPEC:198-202`, which survives the feasibility finding intact: demote the measured rate **from a DPS multiplier to a cast-propensity prior**, which needs correct RELATIVE ordering across spells (preserved by the whole-game basis) and not a correct denominator. This also protects the signal RM-39 flagged as must-not-discard - Aatrox W sits at 17.6% of theoretical because Infernal Chains is genuinely cast less often than available, and a cooldown-inverse model throws that away. **Consequence for sequencing:** `apply_ad_axis_ability_damage` default-ON is no longer gated on RM-98's original framing, because that framing rested on a retracted premise and on a defect three shipped scorers carry. The flip stays operator-gated and is NOT recommended here on its own merits - correction (2), the term being load-bearing at 29.2% cohort mean, is the material input to that decision. **Open hypothesis filed, flagged as unproven:** the recorded "Liandry's #1 / Blackfire #2 for all seven mages" invariance (`DS_SWEEP_TRACKER.md:186-194`) is consistent with always-on item DPS entering `_rank_mage.py:332` at full combat weight while the spell rows it competes against enter at whole-game weight - if so that invariance is partly an ARTIFACT of this defect. Needs its own experiment. **Method note:** four disjoint read-only investigators (provenance archaeology / consumer semantics / hybrid arithmetic / RM-39 dependency), each load-bearing claim independently re-probed before adoption - the arithmetic agent REFUTED the main-thread inertness hypothesis, which is the pass working as intended. Spec: `docs/specs/SPEC_rm98_cast_rate_time_base.md`. Commit `3aaf586f`.

955. DONE **2026-07-19 (RM-39/RM-43 L2 - the AD-axis ability term's credited damage types widened PHYSICAL -> PHYSICAL + TRUE; ENGINE 1.222.0 -> 1.223.0, still DEFAULT-OFF.
